children.text: ity evam uktvā pitaraṃ candra-bhāgā-nadī-jale /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to his father, in the waters of the <s>Candrabhāgā</s> river

children.text: snātvā papau jalaṃ svacchaṃ bubhuje miṣṭa-modakam // Jss_1,3.47 //
children.translated_text: he bathed, drank the clear water, and ate sweet <s>modaka</s> (sweetmeats). (Jss 1.3.47)

children.text: pitā tad-vacanaṃ śrutvā sānandāśru mumoca saḥ /
children.translated_text: The father, having heard those words, shed tears of joy.

children.text: cucumba gaṇḍaṃ putrasya samāśleṣaṇa-pūrvakam // Jss_1,3.48 //
children.translated_text: He kissed the cheek of his son, embracing him first. (Jss 1.3.48)

children.text: pitā snātvā samārebhe sandhyāṃ kartuṃ ca pūjanam /
children.translated_text: The father, having bathed, began to perform the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight prayer) and worship.

children.text: susnātaṃ pitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā putraḥ sa prayayau vanam // Jss_1,3.49 //
children.translated_text: Seeing the father well-bathed, the son went into the forest. (Jss 1.3.49)

children.text: patraṃ bhojana-pātrārtham arhatuṃ cañcalaḥ śiśuḥ /
children.translated_text: The restless child, needing a leaf as a plate for eating,

children.text: cakāra cayanaṃ tūrṇaṃ praśastaṃ patra-pañcakam // Jss_1,3.50 //
children.translated_text: quickly gathered a fine set of five leaves. (Jss 1.3.50)

children.text: sundaraṃ kusumaṃ vanyaṃ pūjanārthaṃ pitus tathā /
children.translated_text: Beautiful wild flowers for his father's worship, and also

children.text: dadarśa purato bālaḥ supakvaṃ vadarī-phalam // Jss_1,3.51 //
children.translated_text: the boy saw before him a ripe <s>vadarī</s> (jujube) fruit. (Jss 1.3.51)

children.text: cakāra cayanaṃ tāni phalāni śobhanāni ca /
children.translated_text: He gathered those beautiful fruits,

children.text: dhātrī-phalaṃ supakvaṃ ca pakvam āmrātakaṃ tathā // Jss_1,3.52 //
children.translated_text: ripe <s>dhātrī</s> (Indian gooseberry) fruits and ripe <s>āmrātaka</s> (hog plum) as well. (Jss 1.3.52)

children.text: supakvaṃ ca kadambaṃ ca cakāra cayanaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: He again gathered ripe <s>kadamba</s> fruits,

children.text: supakvaṃ sundaraṃ ramyaṃ dāḍimaṃ śrī-phalaṃ tathā // Jss_1,3.53 //
children.translated_text: and ripe, beautiful, lovely pomegranates and <s>śrīphala</s> (bilva fruits). (Jss 1.3.53)

children.text: ramyaṃ jambu-phalaṃ caiva kharjūraṃ sumanoharam /
children.translated_text: Lovely <s>jambu</s> (rose apple) fruits, and most delightful dates,

children.text: karañjakaṃ ca jāmbīraṃ sundaraṃ cikuraṃ tathā // Jss_1,3.54 //
children.translated_text: and <s>karañjaka</s>, <s>jāmbīra</s> (citron), and beautiful <s>cikura</s> fruits. (Jss 1.3.54)

children.text: tat sarvaṃ cayanaṃ kṛtvā dadarśa purataḥ saraḥ /
children.translated_text: Having gathered all those, he saw before him a lake,

children.text: sunirmalaṃ jalaṃ svacchaṃ śveta-padmaṃ manoharam // Jss_1,3.55 //
children.translated_text: with pure, clear water and beautiful white lotuses. (Jss 1.3.55)

children.text: ruciraṃ rakta-kahlāraṃ prasphuṭaṃ ca jalāntike /
children.translated_text: Splendid red water-lilies, fully blossomed near the water.

children.text: vihāya tāni sarvāṇi saraḥ-śirasi susthale // Jss_1,3.56 //
children.translated_text: Leaving all those things on the dry bank of the lake, (Jss 1.3.56)

children.text: papau saraḥ-svaccha-toyaṃ jahāra padmam ulvaṇam /
children.translated_text: he drank the clear water of the lake and took an excellent lotus,

children.text: kiṃcit surakta-kahlāraṃ pakvaṃ padma-phalaṃ tathā // Jss_1,3.57 //
children.translated_text: some beautiful red water-lilies, and ripe lotus seeds as well. (Jss 1.3.57)

children.text: sarvam āharaṇaṃ kṛtvā pitaraṃ gantum udyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having gathered everything, he prepared to go to his father,

children.text: praphulla-vadanaḥ śrīmān sasmito dvija-bālakaḥ // Jss_1,3.58 //
children.translated_text: the glorious <s>brāhmaṇa</s> boy, with a radiant face and a smile. (Jss 1.3.58)

children.text: praphulla-campaka-taruṃ dadarśa purataḥ śiśuḥ /
children.translated_text: The child saw before him a fully blossoming <s>campaka</s> tree,

children.text: mallikā-mālatī-kundayūthikā-mādhavī-latāḥ // Jss_1,3.59 //
children.translated_text: and <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine), <s>mālatī</s>, <s>kunda</s>, <s>yūthikā</s>, and <s>mādhavī</s> creepers. (Jss 1.3.59)

children.text: cakāra cayanaṃ sphītaḥ puṣpāṇi sundarāṇi ca /
children.translated_text: He eagerly gathered the beautiful flowers.

children.text: puṣpeṇa phala-patreṇa tasya bhāro babhūva ha // Jss_1,3.60 //
children.translated_text: With the flowers, fruits, and leaves, his load became heavy. (Jss 1.3.60)

children.text: bālo voḍhum aśakyantaś ca yayau gamana-mantharaḥ /
children.translated_text: The boy, unable to carry it all, walked slowly.

children.text: na phalaṃ bubhuje so 'pi dharmādharma-bhayena ca // Jss_1,3.61 //
children.translated_text: He did not eat any fruit, out of fear of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness). (Jss 1.3.61)

children.text: puro dadarśa sa śiśur ghoraṃ vyāghrālayaṃ bhiyā /
children.translated_text: Before him, the child saw a fearsome tiger's lair with dread,

children.text: tāta tāteti śabdaṃ ca cakāra ha punaḥ punaḥ // Jss_1,3.62 //
children.translated_text: and he called out 'Father! Father!' again and again. (Jss 1.3.62)

children.text: na dadarśa ca tātaṃ ca śārdulaṃ ca dadarśa saḥ /
children.translated_text: He did not see his father, but he saw a tiger.

children.text: bhiyā sasmāra govinda-pādāravaindam īpsitam // Jss_1,3.63 //
children.translated_text: In fear, he remembered the beloved lotus feet of <s>Govinda</s>. (Jss 1.3.63)

children.text: hariṃ nara-hariṃ rāmaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ ca mādhvam /
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, <s>Narahari</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>,

children.text: dāmodaraṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ mukundaṃ madhu-sūdanam // Jss_1,3.64 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dāmodara</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Mukunda</s>, <s>Madhusūdana</s> — (Jss 1.3.64)

children.text: etāni daśa nāmāni japan vipra-śiśur bhiyā /
children.translated_text: reciting these ten names in fear, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> child

children.text: prayayau purataḥ śīghraṃ punar eva sarovaram // Jss_1,3.65 //
children.translated_text: quickly went forward once more to the lake. (Jss 1.3.65)

children.text: saraso nirmale tīre puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca /
children.translated_text: On the pure shore of the lake, the flowers and fruits

children.text: dadau bhaktyā bhagavate kṛṣṇāya paramātmane // Jss_1,3.66 //
children.translated_text: he offered with devotion to <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Self. (Jss 1.3.66)

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa-pūjāṃ kurvantaṃ dhyānamānāṃ padāmbujam /
children.translated_text: While performing worship of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> and meditating on his lotus feet,

children.text: nikaṭaṃ na yayau vyāghro dṛṣṭvā bālaṃ ca dūrataḥ // Jss_1,3.67 //
children.translated_text: the tiger did not approach, seeing the boy from afar. (Jss 1.3.67)

children.text: vyāghraṃ dadarśa bālaś ca prakaṭāsyaṃ bhayānakam /
children.translated_text: The boy saw the tiger with gaping jaws, fearsome,

children.text: vikṛtākāra-daśanaṃ vikaṭākṣaṃ mahodaram // Jss_1,3.68 //
children.translated_text: with deformed fangs, terrible eyes, and a huge belly. (Jss 1.3.68)

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca durato vyāghram uvāsa sarasas taṭe /
children.translated_text: Seeing the tiger from a distance, he remained on the bank of the lake

children.text: dadhyau kṛṣṇa-padāmbhojaṃ janma-mṛtyu-jarā-haram // Jss_1,3.69 //
children.translated_text: and meditated on the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, which destroy birth, death, and old age. (Jss 1.3.69)

children.text: mūlādhāraṃ svādhiṣṭhānaṃ maṇipūram anāhatam /
children.translated_text: <s>Mūlādhāra</s>, <s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s>, <s>Maṇipūra</s>, <s>Anāhata</s>,

children.text: viśuddhaṃ ca tathājñākhyaṃ ṣaṭ-cakraṃ ca vibhāvya ca // Jss_1,3.70 //
children.translated_text: <s>Viśuddha</s>, and <s>Ājñā</s> — having visualized the six <s>cakras</s>, (Jss 1.3.70)

children.text: kuṇḍalinyā sva-śaktyā ca sahitaṃ parameśvaram /
children.translated_text: together with <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, his own power, the Supreme Lord

children.text: sahasra-dala-padma-sthaṃ hṛdaye svātmanaḥ prabhum // Jss_1,3.71 //
children.translated_text: seated on the thousand-petaled lotus, the Lord within his own heart — (Jss 1.3.71)

children.text: dadarśa dvibhujaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ pīta-kauśeya-vāsasam /
children.translated_text: he beheld <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with two arms, wearing yellow silk garments,

children.text: sasmitaṃ sundaraṃ śuddhaṃ navīna-jalada-prabham // Jss_1,3.72 //
children.translated_text: smiling, beautiful, pure, with the radiance of a fresh rain-cloud. (Jss 1.3.72)

children.text: koṭi-kandarpa-saundarya-līlā-dhāma-manoharam /
children.translated_text: Enchanting, the abode of the playful beauty of ten million <s>Kandarpas</s> (Cupids),

children.text: koṭi-pārvaṇa-pūrṇendu-prabhā-juṣṭaṃ ca sundaram // Jss_1,3.73 //
children.translated_text: graced with the radiance of ten million full moons at the equinox, beautiful. (Jss 1.3.73)

children.text: sukha-dṛśyaṃ surūpaṃ ca bhaktānugraha-kārakam /
children.translated_text: Pleasant to behold, of beautiful form, bestowing grace upon his devotees,

children.text: candanokṣita-sarvāṅgaṃ ratna-bhūṣaṇa-bhūṣitam // Jss_1,3.74 //
children.translated_text: with all limbs anointed with sandalwood, adorned with jeweled ornaments. (Jss 1.3.74)

children.text: praphulla-padma-nayanaṃ rādhā-vakṣaḥ-sthala-sthitam /
children.translated_text: With eyes like fully blossomed lotuses, resting on the chest of <s>Rādhā</s>,

children.text: mālatī-mālya-sambaddha-cūḍā-cāru-suśobhanam // Jss_1,3.75 //
children.translated_text: beautifully adorned with a crest adorned with a garland of <s>mālatī</s> flowers. (Jss 1.3.75)

children.text: dhṛta-ratnaṃ ratna-padmaṃ dakṣiṇena kareṇa ca /
children.translated_text: Holding a jewel and a jeweled lotus in the right hand,

children.text: vāmena maṇi-nirmāṇa-dīpta-darpaṇam ujjvalam // Jss_1,3.76 //
children.translated_text: and in the left, a brilliant mirror crafted of gems. (Jss 1.3.76)

children.text: kausthubhena maṇīndreṇa cāru-vakṣaḥ-sthalojjvalam // Jss_1,3.77/
children.translated_text: his beautiful chest brilliant with the <s>Kaustubha</s>, the king of gems. (Jss 1.3.77)

children.text: muktārāji-vinindaika-danta-rāji-virājitam /
children.translated_text: Resplendent with rows of teeth that put to shame strings of pearls,

children.text: ājānu-mālatī-mālā-vana-mālā-vibhūṣitam // Jss_1,3.78 //
children.translated_text: adorned with garlands of <s>mālatī</s> flowers and forest garlands reaching to the knees. (Jss 1.3.78)

body.translated_text: With his cheeks resplendent with a pair of jeweled earrings,

children.text: vedānana-sarasvatyā stutaṃ brahmeśa-vanditam /
children.translated_text: Praised by <s>Sarasvatī</s> of the <s>Vedas</s>, saluted by <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: padmāpadmālayā-māyā-saṃsevita-padāmbujam // Jss_1,3.79 //
children.translated_text: whose lotus feet are served by <s>Padmā</s> (Lakṣmī), <s>Padmālayā</s>, and <s>Māyā</s>. (Jss 1.3.79)

children.text: pari-pūrṇatamam brahma paramātmānam īśvaram /
children.translated_text: The most complete <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Self, the Lord,

children.text: nirliptaṃ sākṣi-bhūtaṃ ca bhagavantaṃ sanātanam // Jss_1,3.80 //
children.translated_text: untouched, the witness, the Blessed One, eternal. (Jss 1.3.80)

children.text: sarveśāṃ sarva-rūpaṃ ca sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: The form of all, the cause of all causes,

children.text: puruṣaṃ paramātmaikaṃ pareśaṃ prakṛteḥ paraṃ // Jss_1,3.81 //
children.translated_text: the one Supreme Person, the Supreme Self, the supreme Lord, beyond <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). (Jss 1.3.81)

children.text: evaṃ bhūtaṃ vibhuṃ dṛṣṭvā manasā praṇanāma tam /
children.translated_text: Seeing such an all-pervading Lord, he bowed to him in his mind

children.text: tuṣṭāva parayā bhaktyā tam īśaṃ sampuṭāñjaliḥ // Jss_1,3.82 //
children.translated_text: and praised that Lord with supreme devotion, with hands joined in <s>añjali</s>. (Jss 1.3.82)

children.text: śrī-subhadra uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Subhadra</s> said:

children.text: he nātha darśnaṃ dehi māṃ bhaktaṃ śaraṇāgatam /
children.translated_text: O Lord, grant me your vision, your devoted one who has taken refuge.

children.text: śrīda śrīśa śrī-nivāsa śrī-nidhe śrī-niketana // Jss_1,3.83 //
children.translated_text: O giver of <s>Śrī</s>, Lord of <s>Śrī</s>, abode of <s>Śrī</s>, treasure of <s>Śrī</s>, dwelling of <s>Śrī</s>! (Jss 1.3.83)

children.text: śriyā sevita-pādābja śrī-samutpatti-kāraṇa /
children.translated_text: O you whose lotus feet are served by <s>Śrī</s>, O cause of the arising of <s>Śrī</s>,

children.text: vedānirvacaniyeśa nirīha nirguṇādhipa // Jss_1,3.84 //
children.translated_text: O Lord beyond the description of the <s>Vedas</s>, O desireless one, O Lord beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities)! (Jss 1.3.84)

children.text: sarvādya sarva-nilaya sarva-bīja sanātana /
children.translated_text: The origin of all, the abode of all, the seed of all, the eternal one,

children.text: śānta sarasvatī-kānta nitānta sarva-karmasu // Jss_1,3.85 //
children.translated_text: the peaceful one, the beloved of <s>Sarasvatī</s>, devoted to all actions. (Jss 1.3.85)

children.text: sarvādhāra nirādhāra kāma-pūra parāt para /
children.translated_text: The support of all, without support, fulfiller of desires, beyond the beyond,

children.text: duṣpārāsāra-saṃsāra-karṇa-dhāra namo 'stu te // Jss_1,3.86 //
children.translated_text: the helmsman of the impassable ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> — salutation to you! (Jss 1.3.86)

children.text: ity evam uktvā sa śiśu ruroda ca punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the child wept again and again,

children.text: dhyāyena tat-padāmbhojaṃ śaraṇaṃ ca cakāra saḥ // Jss_1,3.87 //
children.translated_text: meditating on his lotus feet, he took refuge. (Jss 1.3.87)

children.text: iti viprakṛtaṃ stotraṃ tri-sandhyaṃ yaḥ paṭhen naraḥ /
children.translated_text: The person who recites this hymn composed by the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> three times daily

children.text: mucyate sarva-pāpebhyo viṣṇu-lokaṃ sa gacchati // Jss_1,3.88 //
children.translated_text: is freed from all sins and goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. (Jss 1.3.88)

body.text: iti śrī-nārada-pañca-rātre jñānāmṛta-sāre prathamaika-rātre brahma-sanat-kumāra-saṃvāde śrī-kṛṣṇa-mahimopālambhanaṃ nāma tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus in the sacred <s>Nārada Pañcarātra</s>, in the <s>Jñānāmṛtasāra</s>, in the first night, in the dialogue between <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, the third chapter called "The praise of the glory of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>."
In the first night, the fourth chapter.

children.text: brahmovāca
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: brāhmaṇasya stavaṃ śrutvā parituṣṭo janārdanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard the hymn of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Janārdana</s> was greatly pleased.

children.text: kṛpāṃ cakāra bhagavān bhakteśo bhakta-vatsalaḥ // Jss_1,4.1 //
children.translated_text: The Blessed One, the Lord of devotees, fond of his devotees, showed mercy. (Jss 1.4.1)

children.text: etasminn antare tatra bhagavān nanda-nandanaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the meantime, the Blessed One, the son of <s>Nanda</s>,

children.text: nārāyaṇarṣiḥ kṛpayā cājagāma sarovaram // Jss_1,4.2 //
children.translated_text: the sage <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, came to that lake out of compassion. (Jss 1.4.2)

children.text: dadarśa brāhmaṇa-vaṭuṃ tam eva muni-puṅgavam /
children.translated_text: He saw the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> student, that best of sages,

children.text: tejasā sukha-dṛśyena sundaraṃ sumanoharam // Jss_1,4.3 //
children.translated_text: beautiful, most enchanting, pleasant to behold with his radiance. (Jss 1.4.3)

children.text: pīta-vastra-parīdhānaṃ navīna-jalada-prabham /
children.translated_text: Wearing yellow garments, with the radiance of a fresh rain-cloud,

children.text: candanokṣita-sarvāṅgaṃ vana-mālā-vibhūṣitam // Jss_1,4.4 //
children.translated_text: with all limbs anointed with sandalwood, adorned with a forest garland. (Jss 1.4.4)

children.text: prasanna-vadanaṃ śuddhaṃ sasmitaṃ sarva-pūjitam /
children.translated_text: With a serene face, pure, smiling, worshipped by all,

children.text: vibhāntaṃ ca japantaṃ śuddha-sphaṭika-mālayā // Jss_1,4.5 //
children.translated_text: resplendent, reciting with a pure crystal <s>mālā</s> (rosary). (Jss 1.4.5)

children.text: dṛṣṭvā nanāma sahasā śirasā vipra-puṅgavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing him, the foremost <s>brāhmaṇa</s> quickly bowed with his head.

children.text: śubhāśiṣaṃ dadau tasmai datvā śirasi hastakam // Jss_1,4.6 //
children.translated_text: He gave him an auspicious blessing, placing his hand on his head. (Jss 1.4.6)

children.text: tam uvāca muni-śreṣṭhaḥ kṛpayā dīna-vatsalaḥ /
children.translated_text: The best of sages, compassionate and tender toward the humble, spoke to him

children.text: hitaṃ tathyaṃ nīti-sāraṃ pariṇāma-sukhāvaham // Jss_1,4.7 //
children.translated_text: words that were beneficial, truthful, the essence of wisdom, and leading to ultimate happiness. (Jss 1.4.7)

children.text: śrī-nārāyaṇarṣir uvāca
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> said:

children.text: aye vipra mahā-bhāga saphalaṃ jīvanaṃ tava /
children.translated_text: O <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of great fortune, your life is fruitful.

children.text: yasmin kule ca jāto 'si tad-dhanyaṃ supraśaṃsitam // Jss_1,4.8 //
children.translated_text: The family in which you were born — that is blessed and most praiseworthy. (Jss 1.4.8)

children.text: bhaja tvaṃ paramānandaṃ sānandaṃ nanda-nandanam /
children.translated_text: Worship the supremely blissful, joy-giving son of <s>Nanda</s>.

children.text: dhruvaṃ yāsyasi golokaṃ paramānandam īpsitam // Jss_1,4.9 //
children.translated_text: You will certainly go to <s>Goloka</s>, the desired supreme bliss. (Jss 1.4.9)

children.text: tat kulaṃ pāvanaṃ dhanyaṃ yaśasyaṃ ca nirāpadam /
children.translated_text: That family is purifying, blessed, glorious, and free from danger

children.text: yasmin svayaṃ bhavān jātaḥ puṇyaḥ kṛṣṇa-parāyaṇaḥ // Jss_1,4.10 //
children.translated_text: in which you yourself were born, O meritorious one, devoted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. (Jss 1.4.10)

children.text: naivedyaṃ patitaṃ mārge jīrnaṃ śvāpada-bhakṣitam /
children.translated_text: The <s>naivedya</s> (food offering) that had fallen on the road, decayed and eaten by wild beasts —

children.text: bhuktvā tavaiṣā buddhiś ca kṛṣṇa-bhaktir babhūva ca // Jss_1,4.11 //
children.translated_text: by eating that, this devotion to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> arose in you. (Jss 1.4.11)

children.text: kṛṣṇa-naivedya-māhātmyaṃ ko vatsa kathituṃ kṣamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who, dear child, is able to describe the glory of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s <s>naivedya</s>?

children.text: yad vaktuṃ na hi śaktāś ca vedāś catvāra eva ca // Jss_1,4.12 //
children.translated_text: Even the four <s>Vedas</s> are not able to speak of it. (Jss 1.4.12)

children.text: varaṃ vṛṇuṣva bhadraṃ te subhadra dvija-puṅgava /
children.translated_text: Choose a boon, may it be well with you, O <s>Subhadra</s>, O foremost <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: sarvaṃ dātum ahaṃ śakto yat te manasi vāñcchitam // Jss_1,4.13 //
children.translated_text: I am able to give everything that you desire in your mind. (Jss 1.4.13)

children.text: nārāyaṇa-vacaḥ śrutvā tam uvāca śiṣuḥ svayam /
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the child himself spoke,

children.text: punaḥ kampita-sarvāṅgaḥ sāśru-netraḥ puṭāñjaliḥ // Jss_1,4.14 //
children.translated_text: trembling in all his limbs, with tearful eyes and hands joined in <s>añjali</s>. (Jss 1.4.14)

children.text: subhadra uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Subhadra</s> said:

children.text: dehi me kṛṣṇa-pādābje dṛḍhaṃ bhaktiṃ sudurlabham /
children.translated_text: Grant me firm devotion to the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, so rarely obtained,

children.text: tad-dāsyaṃ tat-pade vāsaṃ jarā-mṛtyu-haraṃ param // Jss_1,4.15 //
children.translated_text: servitude to him, residence at his feet, the supreme destroyer of old age and death. (Jss 1.4.15)

children.text: anyaṃ varaṃ na gṛhṇāmi na me kiṃcit prayojanam /
children.translated_text: I do not accept any other boon; I have no need of anything.

children.text: nāhaṃ varārthī kāmī ca rāgī vetana-bhug yathā // Jss_1,4.16 //
children.translated_text: I am not a seeker of boons, nor desirous, nor attached, like a hired servant. (Jss 1.4.16)

children.text: nārāyaṇarṣir uvāca
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> said:

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇo yasya bhaktiś ca tasyātra kiṃ sudurlabham /
children.translated_text: For one who has devotion to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, what here is difficult to obtain?

children.text: aṇimādika-dva-triṃśat-siddhiḥ kara-tale parā // Jss_1,4.17 //
children.translated_text: The supreme thirty-two <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers) beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) are in the palm of his hand. (Jss 1.4.17)

children.text: nirvikalpo dadāty asya naiva gṛhṇāti vaiṣṇavaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> (devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>) gives these without discrimination, and does not take them himself.

children.text: animittāṃ harer bhaktiṃ bhaktā vāñcchanti santatam // Jss_1,4.18 //
children.translated_text: Devotees always desire causeless devotion to <s>Hari</s>. (Jss 1.4.18)

children.text: gṛhāṇa mantraṃ kṛṣṇasya paraṃ kalpa-taruṃ varam /
children.translated_text: Receive the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the supreme wish-fulfilling tree,

children.text: bhaktidaṃ dāsyadaṃ śuddhaṃ karma-mūla-nikṛntanam // Jss_1,4.19 //
children.translated_text: which bestows devotion, grants servitude, is pure, and cuts the root of <s>karma</s>. (Jss 1.4.19)

children.text: lakṣmīr māyā-kāma-bījaṃ ṅe 'ntaṃ kṛṣṇa-padaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>māyā</s>, <s>kāma-bīja</s>, ending with 'ṅe,' then the word '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,'

children.text: vahni-jāyānta-mantraṃ ca mantra-rājaṃ manoharam // Jss_1,4.20 //
children.translated_text: ending with '<s>vahni-jāyā</s>' — this is the king of <s>mantras</s>, most enchanting. (Jss 1.4.20)

children.text: ity evam uktvā tat-karṇe kathayām āsa dakṣiṇe /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the best of sages whispered it

children.text: vāra-trayaṃ muni-śreṣṭhaḥ śuddha-bhāvena putraka // Jss_1,4.21 //
children.translated_text: three times into his right ear, with pure intention, O dear child. (Jss 1.4.21)

children.text: yena stotreṇa tuṣṭāva subhadraḥ parameśvaram /
children.translated_text: The hymn with which <s>Subhadra</s> had praised the Supreme Lord —

children.text: ājñāṃ cakāra sa ṛṣis tad eva paṭhituṃ mudā // Jss_1,4.22 //
children.translated_text: that same sage commanded him to recite it with joy. (Jss 1.4.22)

children.text: kavacaṃ ca dadau tasmai jagan-maṅgala-maṅgalam /
children.translated_text: He also gave him a <s>kavaca</s> (protective armor), the most auspicious of all auspicious things in the world,

children.text: dhyānaṃ ca sāma-vedoktaṃ sarva-pūjā-vidhi-kramam // Jss_1,4.23 //
children.translated_text: the <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) as stated in the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, and the sequence of all worship rituals. (Jss 1.4.23)

children.text: harer dāsyaṃ ca tad-bhaktir goloka-vāsam īpsitam /
children.translated_text: Servitude to <s>Hari</s>, devotion to him, and the desired residence in <s>Goloka</s> —

children.text: janma-dvayāntare caiva karma-bhoga-kṣaye sati // Jss_1,4.24 //
children.translated_text: within two births, upon the exhaustion of <s>karmic</s> enjoyment. (Jss 1.4.24)

children.text: subhadra uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Subhadra</s> said:

children.text: satyaṃ kuru mahā-bhāga varaṃ me yadi dāsyasi /
children.translated_text: Make it true, O great-fortuned one, if you will grant me a boon.

children.text: varaṃ vṛṇomi tat paścāt yan me manasi vāñcchitam // Jss_1,4.25 //
children.translated_text: I will then choose a boon — that which my mind desires. (Jss 1.4.25)

children.text: nārāyaṇarṣir uvāca
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> said:

children.text: oṃ satyaṃ vatsa dāsyāmi varaṃ vṛṇu yathepsitam /
children.translated_text: Oṃ, truly, dear child, I will give it. Choose a boon as you desire.

children.text: mamāśakyaṃ nāsti kiṃcit dātāhaṃ sarva-sampadām // Jss_1,4.26 //
children.translated_text: There is nothing impossible for me; I am the giver of all prosperity. (Jss 1.4.26)

children.text: subhadra uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Subhadra</s> said:

children.text: kaṇṭhe te kiṃ ca kavacaṃ kasya vā sarva-pūjitam /
children.translated_text: What is that <s>kavaca</s> (protective amulet) on your neck, worshipped by all?

children.text: amūlya-ratna-guṭikā-yuktaṃ ca sumanoharam // Jss_1,4.27 //
children.translated_text: It is adorned with priceless gem beads and most enchanting. (Jss 1.4.27)

body.text: kavacaṃ dehi me deva sva-satya-rakṣaṇaṃ kuru /
body.translated_text: Give me that <s>kavaca</s>, O Lord, and keep your pledge of truth.
Having heard the words of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, with throat, lips, and palate parched, // 1.4.28 //

children.text: vaktuṃ na śaktas tad vākyaṃ dadhyau kṛṣṇa-padāmbujam /
children.translated_text: unable to speak those words, he meditated upon the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;

children.text: pradadau guṭikāṃ tasmai novāca kavacaṃ muniḥ // Jss_1,4.29 //
children.translated_text: the sage gave him the pill (<s>guṭikā</s>) but did not recite the <s>kavaca</s> (protective mantra). // 1.4.29 //

children.text: tam uvāca maharṣiś ca vituṣṭaś conmanāḥ suta /
children.translated_text: The great sage, displeased yet elated, spoke to him, 'O son,

children.text: vatsa krodho hi devasya varaṃ tulyaṃ ca vāñcchitam // Jss_1,4.30 //
children.translated_text: the anger of the Lord is indeed equal to a boon and [fulfills] one's desire.' // 1.4.30 //

children.text: nārāyaṇarṣir uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> the sage said:

children.text: triṃṣat-sahasra-varṣaṃ ca bhuṅkṣva rājyaṃ sudurlabham /
children.translated_text: 'For thirty thousand years, enjoy a kingdom most difficult to obtain;

children.text: labhasva durlabhāṃ lakṣmīṃ māyayā mohito bhava // Jss_1,4.31 //
children.translated_text: obtain rare prosperity (<s>Lakṣmī</s>); be deluded by <s>māyā</s> (illusion). // 1.4.31 //

children.text: mad-iṣṭa-deva-kavacaṃ gṛhītaṃ yena hetunā /
children.translated_text: Since the <s>kavaca</s> of my chosen deity has been taken [by you],

children.text: sapta-kalpānta-jīvasya paratra ca bhaviṣyati // Jss_1,4.32 //
children.translated_text: for one who lives until the end of seven <s>kalpas</s>, there shall be [reward] in the hereafter as well. // 1.4.32 //

children.text: sucireṇaiva kālena golokaṃ ca prāyasyasi /
children.translated_text: After a very long time, you shall go to <s>Goloka</s>;

children.text: pare mṛkaṇḍu-putras tvaṃ mārkaṇḍeyo bhaviṣyasi // Jss_1,4.33 //
children.translated_text: in the next [birth], you, as the son of <s>Mṛkaṇḍu</s>, shall become <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>. // 1.4.33 //

children.text: mayā dattaṃ ca kavacaṃ tvāṃ ca rakṣati putraka /
children.translated_text: The <s>kavaca</s> given by me shall protect you, dear child,

children.text: tava kaṇṭhe sthitiś cāśya prati janmani janmani // Jss_1,4.34 //
children.translated_text: and it shall remain at your throat in birth after birth.' // 1.4.34 //

children.text: punaś ca guṭikā-yuktaṃ kṛtvā ca kavacaṃ muniḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the sage, having again joined the pill (<s>guṭikā</s>) with the <s>kavaca</s>,

children.text: gale dadhāra bhaktyā ca tad-bhakto dharma-nandanaḥ // Jss_1,4.35 //
children.translated_text: placed it at his throat with devotion — that devotee of him, <s>Dharmanandana</s>. // 1.4.35 //

children.text: varaṃ datvā ca sa munir yayau gehaṃ sa unmanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having bestowed the boon, the sage, elated, went to his abode,

children.text: viprāya kavacaṃ datvā naṣṭa-vatsā gaur yathā // Jss_1,4.36 //
children.translated_text: having given the <s>kavaca</s> to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — like a cow that has lost her calf. // 1.4.36 //

children.text: bhrātrā nareṇa pitrā ca dharmeṇa ca mahātmanā /
children.translated_text: By his brother <s>Nara</s>, by his father <s>Dharma</s> the great-souled one,

children.text: mātrā mūrtyā ca patnyā ca śāntyā ca bhartsito muniḥ // Jss_1,4.37 //
children.translated_text: by his mother <s>Mūrti</s>, by his wife <s>Śānti</s>, the sage was reproached. // 1.4.37 //

children.text: vipraḥ samprāpya kavacaṃ mantraṃ kalpa-taruṃ param /
children.translated_text: The <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having obtained the <s>kavaca</s> and the supreme <s>mantra</s> — a wish-fulfilling tree (<s>kalpa-taru</s>) —

children.text: sarovarāt samutthāya prajvalan brahma-tejasā // Jss_1,4.38 //
children.translated_text: rose from the lake, blazing with the radiance of <s>Brahman</s>. // 1.4.38 //

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ tasthau saras-tīre vaṭa-mūle manohare /
children.translated_text: He stood for a moment on the bank of the lake at the base of a beautiful banyan tree,

children.text: jajāpa paramaṃ mantraṃ sampūjya jagad-īśvaram // Jss_1,4.39 //
children.translated_text: and chanted the supreme <s>mantra</s>, having worshipped the Lord of the universe. // 1.4.39 //

children.text: atha tat-tāta-vipro hi samanviṣya sutaṃ ciram /
children.translated_text: Then his father, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having searched for his son for a long time,

children.text: gatvā ca sva-gṛhaṃ duḥkhī śokārtaḥ sa ruroda ca // Jss_1,4.40 //
children.translated_text: went to his own house, sorrowful and grief-stricken, and wept. // 1.4.40 //

children.text: samudyatā tanuṃ tyaktuṃ tan-mātā putra-vārtayā /
children.translated_text: His mother was about to give up her body upon [hearing] the news of her son,

children.text: na tatyāja tanuṃ vipro dṛṣṭvā susvapnam uttamam // Jss_1,4.41 //
children.translated_text: but the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> did not abandon his body, having seen an excellent auspicious dream. // 1.4.41 //

children.text: vipro viprā gṛhaṃ tyaktvā putrānveṣaṇa-pūrvakam /
children.translated_text: The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and the <s>brāhmaṇī</s>, leaving the house, in search of their son,

children.text: prayayau kānanaṃ ghoraṃ sarvaiś ca bāndhavaiḥ sahaḥ // Jss_1,4.42 //
children.translated_text: went to the terrible forest together with all their kinsmen. // 1.4.42 //

children.text: sarvaṃ vanaṃ samanviṣya prayayus te sarovaram /
children.translated_text: Having searched the entire forest, they came to the lake;

children.text: dadṛśus te śiśuṃ gṛhyaṃ sūryābhaṃ vaṭa-mūlake // Jss_1,4.43 //
children.translated_text: they beheld the child at the base of the banyan tree, radiant like the sun. // 1.4.43 //

children.text: cucumba gaṇḍaṃ putrasya vipro viprā ca sāradam /
children.translated_text: The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and the <s>brāhmaṇī</s> kissed the cheek of their son with delight;

children.text: āśiśleṣa krameṇaiva mātā tātaḥ punaḥ punaḥ // Jss_1,4.44 //
children.translated_text: the mother and father embraced [him] in turn, again and again. // 1.4.44 //

children.text: putraś ca sarva-vṛttāntaṃ kathayām āsa sādaram /
children.translated_text: The son narrated the entire account with respect;

children.text: śrutvā putrasya vipraś ca viprā bāndhavas tathā // Jss_1,4. 45 //
children.translated_text: having heard [it], the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇī</s>, and the kinsmen likewise, // 1.4.45 //

children.text: yayuḥ sarve sva-deśaṃ ca paramāhlāda-mānasāḥ /
children.translated_text: all went to their own country with minds filled with supreme delight;

children.text: candra-bhāgāṃ samuttīrya viveśa nagaraṃ param // Jss_1,4.46 //
children.translated_text: having crossed the <s>Candrabhāgā</s> [river], they entered the great city. // 1.4.46 //

children.text: nagara-stho nṛpendraś ca dṛṣṭvā tejasvinaṃ śiśum /
children.translated_text: The king residing in the city, upon seeing the radiant child,

children.text: dadau tasmai sva-kanyāṃ ca ratnālaṅkāra-bhūṣitam // Jss_1,4.47 //
children.translated_text: gave to him his own daughter, adorned with jeweled ornaments, // 1.4.47 //

children.text: yuvatīṃ sundarīṃ śyāmāṃ tapta-kañcana-saṃnibhām /
children.translated_text: a young, beautiful, dark-complexioned maiden resembling molten gold,

children.text: pati-vratāṃ mahā-bhāgāṃ sundarīṃ kamalākalāṃ // Jss_1,4.48 //
children.translated_text: devoted to her husband, greatly fortunate, beautiful, with the grace of a lotus. // 1.4.48 //

children.text: gajendrāṇāṃ sahasraṃ ca pradadau yautukaṃ mudā /
children.translated_text: He gave with joy as dowry a thousand lordly elephants,

children.text: aśvānāṃ daśa-lakṣaṃ ca ratnānāṃ ca sahasrakam // Jss_1,4.49 //
children.translated_text: ten hundred-thousand horses, and a thousand [sets of] jewels, // 1.4.49 //

children.text: dāsīnāṃ niṣka-kaṇṭhīnāṃ saundarīṇāṃ sahasrakam /
children.translated_text: a thousand beautiful maidservants wearing gold necklaces,

children.text: vastra-ratna-sahasraṃ ca bahu-mūlyaṃ sudurlabham // Jss_1,4.50 //
children.translated_text: a thousand [pieces of] garments and jewels, of great value and most rare, // 1.4.50 //

children.text: dāsānāṃ ca sahasraṃ ca padātīnāṃ tri-lakṣakam /
children.translated_text: a thousand male servants, three hundred-thousand foot soldiers,

children.text: daśa-lakṣaṃ suvarṇaṃ ca ratna-mālāṃ sudurlabhām // Jss_1,4.51 //
children.translated_text: ten hundred-thousand [coins of] gold, and a jeweled garland most rare. // 1.4.51 //

children.text: datvā tasmai ca kanyāṃ ca ruroda ca sabhāryakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having given his daughter to him, the king wept together with his wife;

children.text: rājā ca kanyayā sārdhaṃ prayayau vipra-mandiram // Jss_1,4.52 //
children.translated_text: the king, together with [his] daughter, proceeded to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s dwelling. // 1.4.52 //

children.text: gatvā cāpi kiyad dūraṃ dadarśa nagaraṃ nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having gone some distance, the king saw a city

children.text: atīva sundaraṃ ramyaṃ vijitya cāmarāvatīm // Jss_1,4.53 //
children.translated_text: exceedingly beautiful and charming, surpassing <s>Amarāvatī</s>. // 1.4.53 //

children.text: śuddha-sphaṭika-saṃkāśaṃ ratna-sāra-vinirmitam /
children.translated_text: Resembling pure crystal, constructed of the finest gems,

children.text: tri-koṭi-caṭṭālikā-gehaṃ nava-koṭi-sumandiram // Jss_1,4.54 //
children.translated_text: with thirty million palatial houses and ninety million excellent mansions, // 1.4.54 //

children.text: sapta-prākāra-yuktaṃ ca parikhā-traya-samyuktam /
children.translated_text: equipped with seven ramparts and three moats,

children.text: durlaṅghyam ati-durgamyaṃ ripūṇām api putraka // Jss_1,4.55 //
children.translated_text: impregnable and utterly inaccessible even to enemies, O son. // 1.4.55 //

children.text: śiśoś ca svāśramaṃ ramyaṃ sad-ratna-sāra-nirmitam /
children.translated_text: The child's beautiful hermitage was constructed of the finest gems,

children.text: sphurat vajra-kapāṭaṃ ca ratnendra-kalaśānvitam // Jss_1,4.56 //
children.translated_text: with glistening diamond gates and pinnacle-vessels of the king of gems, // 1.4.56 //

children.text: sad-ratna-darpaṇāir dīpaṃ ratna-kumbhair virājitam /
children.translated_text: illuminated by mirrors of fine gems and adorned with gem-studded vessels,

children.text: prāṅgaṇaṃ ratna-sārāḍhyaṃ ratna-sopāna-śobhitam // Jss_1,4.57 //
children.translated_text: its courtyard resplendent with fine gems, beautified with staircases of gems. // 1.4.57 //

children.text: manoharaṃ rāja-mārgaṃ sindūrādi-pariṣkṛtam /
children.translated_text: The charming royal highway was adorned with vermillion and the like;

children.text: prākāraṃ maṇi-bhūṣāḍhyam uccair ākāśa-sparśi ca // Jss_1,4.58 //
children.translated_text: the rampart, rich with jewel-ornaments, soared high, touching the sky. // 1.4.58 //

children.text: jagāma vismayaṃ rājā dṛṣṭvā nagaram uttamam /
children.translated_text: The king was astonished upon seeing the magnificent city;

children.text: pitrā mātrā saha śiśur vismayaṃ ca yayau mudā // Jss_1,4.59 //
children.translated_text: the child, together with his father and mother, was filled with wonder and joy. // 1.4.59 //

children.text: gajendrāṇāṃ tri-lakṣaṃ ca śvānāṃ śata-lakṣakam /
children.translated_text: Three hundred-thousand lordly elephants, ten million horses,

children.text: catur-guṇaṃ padātīnām āyayus te 'py anuvrajam // Jss_1,4.60 //
children.translated_text: and fourfold [that number] of foot soldiers came following in procession. // 1.4.60 //

children.text: vāraṇendraṃ puras kṛtya veśyāṃ ca nartakaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Placing at the fore the best elephant, courtesans, and dancers,

children.text: dvijāṃś ca pūrṇa-kumbhāṃś ca pati-putravatīṃ satīṃ // Jss_1,4.61 //
children.translated_text: as well as <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, vessels filled [with auspicious substances], and faithful women whose husbands and sons were living, // 1.4.61 //

children.text: mahā-pātraḥ śiśuṃ dṛṣṭvā gajendropari-saṃsthitam /
children.translated_text: the chief minister (<s>mahā-pātra</s>), upon seeing the child seated atop the lordly elephant,

children.text: mūrdhnā nanāma vegenāpy avaruhya gajād api // Jss_1,4.62 //
children.translated_text: bowed his head and swiftly dismounted from [his own] elephant. // 1.4.62 //

children.text: śiśuṃ praveśayāṃ āsa ratna-nirmāṇa-mandiram /
children.translated_text: He ushered the child into the palace built of gems

children.text: ratna-siṃhāsanaṃ tasmai pradadau sādaraṃ mudā // Jss_1,4.63 //
children.translated_text: and respectfully and joyfully offered him a jeweled throne. // 1.4.63 //

children.text: kanyā-dātre ca pitre ca mātre ca sādaraṃ mudā /
children.translated_text: To the father who had given his daughter, to the [boy's own] father and mother, respectfully and joyfully,

children.text: ratna-siṃḥāsanaṃ ramyaṃ pradadau pātra eva ca // Jss_1,4.64 //
children.translated_text: the minister offered beautiful jeweled thrones as well. // 1.4.64 //

children.text: śiśum siṣeva pātraś ca svayaṃ ca śveta-cāmaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: The minister himself served the child with white <s>cāmara</s> (fly-whisks)

children.text: dadhāra ratna-chatraṃ ca hīrāhāra-pariṣkṛtam // Jss_1,4.65 //
children.translated_text: and held over him a jeweled parasol adorned with diamond garlands. // 1.4.65 //

children.text: uvāsa sa sa-bhāryāṃ ca sudharmyāṃ mahendravat /
children.translated_text: He dwelt with his wife in the <s>Sudharmā</s> (assembly hall) like great <s>Indra</s>;

children.text: śvasuraś ca yayau gehaṃ śiśunā ca puraskṛtaḥ // Jss_1,4.66 //
children.translated_text: and the father-in-law went to his [own] home, honored by the child. // 1.4.66 //

children.text: triṃśat-sahasra-varṣaṃ ca rājā rājyaṃ cakāra saḥ /
children.translated_text: For thirty thousand years, he reigned as king;

children.text: kālāntare tat-pitā ca vane vyāghreṇa bhakṣitaḥ // Jss_1,4.67 //
children.translated_text: in the course of time, his father was devoured by a tiger in the forest. // 1.4.67 //

children.text: pati-vratā mahā-bhāgā mātā saha-mṛtā suta /
children.translated_text: His devoted and greatly fortunate mother died along [with the father], O son;

children.text: ratna-yānena ramyeṇa sa-strīkaḥ kṛṣṇa-mandiram // Jss_1,4.68 //
children.translated_text: in a beautiful jeweled chariot, with his wife, to the abode of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, // 1.4.68 //

children.text: prayayau sādaraṃ vipraḥ kṛṣṇa-naivedya-bhakṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> proceeded with devotion, due to having eaten <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s <s>naivedya</s> (food offering);

children.text: tad-asthi bhuktvā vyāghraś ca pūtaḥ sadyaś ca sāṃpratam // Jss_1,4.69 //
children.translated_text: and the tiger, having eaten those bones, was at once purified forthwith. // 1.4.69 //

children.text: tābhyāṃ sārdhaṃ ca prayayau golokaṃ sumanoharam /
children.translated_text: Together with both [parents], he proceeded to the most delightful <s>Goloka</s>;

children.text: śiśur dehaṃ parityajya himādrau svar-ṇadī-taṭe // Jss_1,4.70 //
children.translated_text: the child, abandoning his body on the <s>Himālaya</s>, on the bank of the heavenly <s>Gaṅgā</s>, // 1.4.70 //

children.text: datvā putrāya rājyaṃ ca svargād api sudurlabham /
children.translated_text: having given the kingdom to his son — [a kingdom] more difficult to obtain than heaven itself —

children.text: mṛkaṇḍu-patnī-garbhe ca lebhe janma sva-karmaṇā // Jss_1,4.71 //
children.translated_text: took birth in the womb of <s>Mṛkaṇḍu</s>'s wife through his own <s>karma</s>. // 1.4.71 //

children.text: mārkaṇḍeyo muni-śreṣṭho babhūva para-janmani /
children.translated_text: <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, the best of sages, he became in the next birth,

children.text: sapta-kalpānta-jīvī ca nārāyaṇa-vareṇa saḥ // Jss_1,4.72 //
children.translated_text: living until the end of seven <s>kalpas</s>, by the boon of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. // 1.4.72 //

body.text:
babhūva sāṃprataṃ vipraḥ kṛṣṇa-naivedya-bhakṣaṇāt /
śva-bhakṣitaṃ ca naivedyaṃ bhuktvā ced īdṛśī gatiḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> became [all this] now, due to having eaten <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s <s>naivedya</s>; if such is the destiny from eating <s>naivedya</s> that was eaten by a dog,

body.text: akāmataś cāpy ajñāto jīrṇa-mārga-sthitaṃ suta // Jss_1,4.73 //
body.translated_text: unknowingly, unintentionally, [food] placed on an old path, O son — // 1.4.73 //

children.text: yo bhakṣet kāmato jñāto nityaṃ naivedyam īpsitam /
children.translated_text: for one who eats knowingly, intentionally, the desired <s>naivedya</s> daily,

children.text: na jānanti gatis tasya vedāś catvāra eva ca // Jss_1,4.74 //
children.translated_text: even the four <s>Vedas</s> do not know his destiny. // 1.4.74 //

children.text: iti te kathitaṃ brahmann itihāsaṃ purātanam /
children.translated_text: Thus I have narrated to you, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, this ancient <s>itihāsa</s> (history),

children.text: āścaryaṃ madhuraṃ ramyaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi // Jss_1,4.75 //
children.translated_text: wondrous, sweet, and delightful — what more do you wish to hear? // 1.4.75 //

children.text: śrī-nārada uvāca
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: śrutaṃ naivedya-māhātmyam atīva sumanoharam /
children.translated_text: I have heard the glory of the <s>naivedya</s>, exceedingly delightful,

children.text: īśvarasyāpi he tāta kṛṣṇasya paramātmanaḥ // Jss_1,4.76 //
children.translated_text: of the Lord himself, O father, of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Self. // 1.4.76 //

children.text: adhunā śrotum icchāmi svātma-sandeha-bhañjanam /
children.translated_text: Now I wish to hear that which dispels my own doubt —

children.text: nārāyaṇarṣer kaṇṭhe ca kavacaṃ tasya tad vada // Jss_1,4.77 //
children.translated_text: tell me of the <s>kavaca</s> that is at the throat of the sage <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. // 1.4.77 //

body.translated_text: Now, the question about the <s>kavaca</s>:

children.text: sanat-kumāra uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: mamāpy astīti sandeho vacane prapitāmaha /
children.translated_text: 'I too have a doubt, O great-grandfather, about [your] words;

children.text: kasya tat kavacaṃ brahmann idaṃ vaktuṃ tvam arhasi // Jss_1,4.78 //
children.translated_text: whose is that <s>kavaca</s>, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>? Please tell this. // 1.4.78 //

children.text: sa pitā sa guruḥ svacchaḥ karoti bhrama-bhañjanam /
children.translated_text: He is [both] father and <s>guru</s>, transparent, who dispels delusion;

children.text: śīghraṃ brūhi mahā-bhāga nāradaṃ māṃ suta-priya // Jss_1,4.79 //
children.translated_text: speak quickly, O greatly fortunate one, to me, <s>Nārada</s>, who is dear as a son.' // 1.4.79 //

children.text: putrayoś ca vacaḥ śrutvā śuṣka-kaṇṭhauṣṭhatālukaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of both sons, with throat, lips, and palate parched,

children.text: uvāca vacanaṃ brahmā smaran kṛṣṇa-padāmbujam // Jss_1,4.80 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> spoke these words, remembering the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: // 1.4.80 //

children.text: brahmovāca
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: nārāyaṇena muninā jagan-maṅgala-maṅgalam /
children.translated_text: 'By the sage <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the auspiciousness of all auspiciousness in the universe,

children.text: viprāya kavacaṃ dattam dhyānaṃ ca parmātmanaḥ // Jss_1,4.81 //
children.translated_text: the <s>kavaca</s> was given to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, along with the meditation on the Supreme Self. // 1.4.81 //

children.text: tad bravīmi mahā-bhāga tvām eva nāradaṃ prati /
children.translated_text: I shall tell it to you, O greatly fortunate <s>Nārada</s>;

children.text: kaṇṭha-sthaṃ kavacaṃ vaktuṃ naiva śaknomi sāṃpratam // Jss_1,4.82 //
children.translated_text: but the <s>kavaca</s> that resides at my throat — I am unable to recite it now. // 1.4.82 //

children.text: mat-kaṇṭhe kavacaṃ yasya gopanīyaṃ sudurlabham /
children.translated_text: The <s>kavaca</s> at my throat is most secret and exceedingly rare;

children.text: nārāyaṇarṣi-kaṇṭhe ca tad eva paramādbhutam // Jss_1,4.83 //
children.translated_text: the very same is at the throat of the sage <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — most wonderful. // 1.4.83 //

children.text: tad eva dharma-kaṇṭhe ca narasya ca mahātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: That same is at the throat of <s>Dharma</s> and of the great-souled <s>Nara</s>,

children.text: agastyasya ca kaṇṭhe ca lomaśasya mahā-muneḥ // Jss_1,4.84 //
children.translated_text: and at the throat of <s>Agastya</s>, and of the great sage <s>Lomaśa</s>. // 1.4.84 //

children.text: tulasyāś cāpi saṃjñāyāḥ sāvitryāś cāpi putraka /
children.translated_text: And of her known as <s>Tulasī</s>, and of <s>Sāvitrī</s> as well, O son,

children.text: anyeṣāṃ ca bhāgyavatāṃ bhārate ca sudurlabhe // Jss_1,4.85 //
children.translated_text: and of other fortunate ones — [it is] most rare in <s>Bhārata</s>.' // 1.4.85 //

children.text: nārada uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: paścāt śroṣyāmi kavacaṃ jagan-maṅgala-maṅgalam /
children.translated_text: 'Later I shall hear the <s>kavaca</s>, the auspiciousness of all auspiciousness in the universe;

children.text: dhyānaṃ pūjāṃ vidhānaṃ ca kṛṣṇasya paramātmanaḥ // Jss_1,4.86 //
children.translated_text: [as well as] the meditation, worship, and ritual procedure of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Self. // 1.4.86 //

children.text: ādau kathaya bhadraṃ te paraṃ parama-bhadrakam /
children.translated_text: First, may it be auspicious for you — tell me the supremely auspicious

children.text: subhadra-prāptaṃ kavacaṃ māhātmyaṃ yasya durlabham // Jss_1,4.87 //
children.translated_text: <s>kavaca</s> obtained by <s>Subhadra</s>, whose glory is rare [to find]. // 1.4.87 //'

children.text: brahmovāca
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: subhadra-prāptaṃ kavacaṃ paścāt śroṣyasi putraka /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>kavaca</s> obtained by <s>Subhadra</s> — you shall hear it later, O son;

children.text: śaṅkarasya mukhād vipra sva-guror jñāninas tathā // Jss_1,4.88 //
children.translated_text: [it came] from the mouth of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s own <s>guru</s>, the knower.' // 1.4.88 //

body.text:
iti śrī-nārada-pañca-rātre jñānāmṛta-sāre brahmā-nārada-saṃvāde
prathamaika-rātre kavaca-praśno nāma caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter, called 'The Question about the <s>Kavaca</s>,' in the dialogue between <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Nārada</s>, in the first night of the <s>Jñānāmṛtasāra</s> within the <s>Nārada Pañcarātra</s>.
Fifth chapter of the first night.

children.text: śrī-sanat-kumāra uvāca
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: tavecchā yatra kavace dhyāne tad vada sāmpratam /
children.translated_text: 'Your wish regarding the <s>kavaca</s> and the meditation — tell it now;

children.text: yac chṛṇomi śubhaṃ tac ca kena śreyasi tṛpyate // Jss_1,5.1 //
children.translated_text: whatever auspicious thing I hear — by what [other] blessing could one be satisfied? // 1.5.1 //'

children.text: bramovāca
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: dhyānaṃ sāma-vedoktaṃ dattam nārāyaṇena vai /
children.translated_text: 'The meditation as stated in the <s>Sāma Veda</s> was given by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> indeed,

children.text: kavacaṃ ca subhadrāya dharmiṣṭhāya mahātmane // Jss_1,5.2 //
children.translated_text: together with the <s>kavaca</s>, to <s>Subhadra</s>, the righteous and great-souled one. // 1.5.2 //

children.text: navīna-jalada-śyāmaṃ pīta-kauśeya-vāsasam /
children.translated_text: Dark as a fresh rain-cloud, wearing yellow silken garments,

children.text: candanokṣita-sarvāṅgaṃ sasmitaṃ śyāmasundaram // Jss_1,5.3 //
children.translated_text: all limbs anointed with sandalwood, smiling, the beautiful dark one (<s>Śyāmasundara</s>), // 1.5.3 //

children.text: mālatī-mālya-bhūṣāḍhyaṃ ratna-bhūṣaṇa-bhūṣitam /
children.translated_text: adorned with garlands of <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine), bedecked with jeweled ornaments,

children.text: munīndreśa-susiddheśa-brahmeśa-śeṣa-vanditam // Jss_1,5.4 //
children.translated_text: venerated by the lords of sages, the lords of <s>siddhas</s>, by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śeṣa</s>, and all, // 1.5.4 //

children.text: sarva-svarūpaṃ sarveśaṃ sarva-bījaṃ sanātanam /
children.translated_text: the form of all, Lord of all, seed of all, eternal,

children.text: sarvādyaṃ sarva-jñaṃ puruṣaṃ prakṛteḥ param // Jss_1,5.5 //
children.translated_text: the origin of all, omniscient, the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person) beyond <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), // 1.5.5 //

children.text: nirguṇaṃ ca nirīhaṃ ca nirliptam īsvaraṃ bhaje /
children.translated_text: without qualities, without desires, untainted — I worship that Lord. Having meditated [thus] with the root [<s>mantra</s>], one should joyfully offer <s>pādya</s> (water for the feet) and the like to Him,

children.text: dhyātvā mūlena tasmai ca dadyāt pādyādikaṃ mudā // Jss_1,5.6 //
tataḥ stotraṃ ca kavacaṃ bhaktyā ca prapaṭhen naraḥ /
children.translated_text: then a person should recite with devotion the hymn and the <s>kavaca</s>;

children.text: japtvā ca mantraṃ bhaktyā daṇḍavat praṇamed bhuvi /
children.translated_text: having chanted the <s>mantra</s> with devotion, one should prostrate on the ground like a staff (<s>daṇḍavat</s>).

children.text: iti te kathitaṃ vatsa kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi // Jss_1,5.7 //
children.translated_text: Thus I have told you, dear child — what more do you wish to hear? // 1.5.7 //'

children.text: śrī-sanatkumāra uvāca
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: brūhi me kavacaṃ brahman jagan-maṅgala-maṅgalam /
children.translated_text: 'Tell me the <s>kavaca</s>, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the auspiciousness of all auspiciousness in the universe —'

children.text: pūjyaṃ puṇya-svarūpaṃ ca kṛṣṇasya paramātmanaḥ // Jss_1,5.8 //
children.translated_text: worthy of worship, of meritorious form, belonging to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Self. // Jss_1,5.8 //

body.translated_text: Now, the auspicious protective armor (<s>kavaca</s>) that brings blessing to the universe:

children.text: brahmovāca
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu vakṣyāmi viprendra kavacaṃ paramādbhutaṃ /
children.translated_text: Listen, I shall speak, O best of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the protective armor (<s>kavaca</s>), most wondrous,

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇenaiva kathitaṃ mahyaṃ ca kṛpayā parā // Jss_1,5.9 //
children.translated_text: which <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself narrated to me, out of supreme compassion. // Jss_1,5.9 //

children.text: mayā dattaṃ ca dharmāya tena nārāyaṇarṣaye /
children.translated_text: By me it was given to <s>Dharma</s>, and by him to the sage <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;

children.text: ṛṣiṇā tena tad dattaṃ subhadrāya mahātmane // Jss_1,5.10 //
children.translated_text: by that sage it was given to the great-souled <s>Subhadrā</s>. // Jss_1,5.10 //

children.text: ati-guhyatamaṃ śuddhaṃ paraṃ snehād vadāmy aham /
children.translated_text: Most supremely secret, pure, and supreme — out of affection I speak it.

children.text: yad dhṛtvā paṭhanāt siddhāḥ siddhāni prāpnuvanti ca // Jss_1,5.11 //
children.translated_text: By wearing and reciting it, <s>Siddhas</s> attain <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers). // Jss_1,5.11 //

children.text: evam indrādayaḥ sarve sarvaiśvaryam āpnuyuḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Indra</s> and all the others obtained all sovereignty.

children.text: ṛṣiś chandaś ca sāvitrī devo nārāyaṇaḥ svayam // Jss_1,5.12 //
children.translated_text: The <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) and meter are <s>Sāvitrī</s>; the deity is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> Himself. // Jss_1,5.12 //

children.text: dharmārtha-kāma-mokṣeṣu viniyogaḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Its application is declared for <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).

children.text: rādheśo me śiraḥ pātu kaṇṭhaṃ radheśvaraḥ // Jss_1,5.13 //
children.translated_text: May the Lord of <s>Rādhā</s> protect my head; may <s>Rādheśvara</s> (the Lord of <s>Rādhā</s>) protect my throat. // Jss_1,5.13 //

children.text: gopīśaś cakṣuṣī pātu tālu ca bhagavān svayam /
children.translated_text: May the Lord of the <s>Gopīs</s> protect my eyes; may the Blessed One Himself protect my palate.

children.text: gaṇḍa-yugmaṃ ca govindaḥ karṇa-yugmaṃ ca keśavaḥ // Jss_1,5.14 //
children.translated_text: May <s>Govinda</s> protect both my cheeks; may <s>Keśava</s> protect both my ears. // Jss_1,5.14 //

children.text: galaṃ gadādharaḥ pātu skandhaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ svayaṃ prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: May <s>Gadādhara</s> (the mace-bearer) protect my neck; may <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself, the Lord, protect my shoulders.

children.text: vakṣa-sthalaṃ vāsudevaś codaraṃ cāpi so 'cyutaḥ // Jss_1,5.15 //
children.translated_text: May <s>Vāsudeva</s> protect my chest; and may <s>Acyuta</s> (the Infallible One) protect my belly. // Jss_1,5.15 //

children.text: nabhiṃ pātu padma-nābhaḥ kaṅkālaṃ kaṃsa-sūdanaḥ /
children.translated_text: May <s>Padmanābha</s> (the lotus-naveled) protect my navel; may <s>Kaṃsasūdana</s> (the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>) protect my skeleton.

children.text: puruṣottamaḥ pātu pṛṣṭhaṃ nityānando nitambakam // Jss_1,5.16 //
children.translated_text: May <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person) protect my back; may <s>Nityānanda</s> (Eternal Bliss) protect my hips. // Jss_1,5.16 //

children.text: puṇḍarīkaḥ pāda-yugmaṃ hasta-yugmaṃ hariḥ svayam /
children.translated_text: May <s>Puṇḍarīka</s> (the Lotus-eyed) protect both my feet; may <s>Hari</s> Himself protect both my hands.

children.text: nāsāṃ ca nakharaṃ pātu narasiṃhaḥ svayaṃ prabhuḥ // Jss_1,5.17 //
children.translated_text: May Lord <s>Narasiṃha</s> (the Man-Lion) Himself protect my nose and nails. // Jss_1,5.17 //

children.text: sarveśvaraś ca sarvāṅgaṃ santataṃ madhu-sūdanaḥ /
children.translated_text: May the Lord of all, <s>Madhusūdana</s> (the slayer of <s>Madhu</s>), perpetually protect all my limbs.

children.text: prācyāṃ pātu ca rāmaś ca vahnau ca vaṃśī-dharaḥ svayam // Jss_1,5.18 //
children.translated_text: May <s>Rāma</s> protect in the east; and may the flute-bearer (<s>Vaṃśīdhara</s>) Himself protect in the direction of fire (southeast). // Jss_1,5.18 //

children.text: pātu dāmodaro dakṣe nairṛte ca narottmaḥ /
children.translated_text: May <s>Dāmodara</s> protect in the south; may <s>Narottama</s> (the Best of Men) protect in the southwest.

children.text: paścime puṇḍarīkākṣo vāyavyāṃ vāmanaḥ svayam // Jss_1,5.19 //
children.translated_text: May <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s> (the Lotus-eyed) protect in the west; may <s>Vāmana</s> Himself protect in the northwest. // Jss_1,5.19 //

children.text: anantaś cottare pātu aiśānyām īśvaraḥ svayam /
children.translated_text: May <s>Ananta</s> (the Infinite) protect in the north; may <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) Himself protect in the northeast.

children.text: jale sthale cāntarīkṣe svapne jāgaraṇe tathā // Jss_1,5.20 //
children.translated_text: In water, on land, in the atmosphere, in sleep and in waking — // Jss_1,5.20 //

children.text: pātu vṛndāvaneśaś ca māṃ bhaktaṃ śaraṇāgatam /
children.translated_text: may the Lord of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> protect me, His devotee who has taken refuge.

children.text: iti te kathitaṃ vatsa kavacaṃ paramādbhutam // Jss_1,5.21 //
children.translated_text: Thus has been told to you, O child, the protective armor, most wondrous, // Jss_1,5.21 //

children.text: sukhadaṃ mokṣadaṃ sāraṃ sarva-siddhi-pradaṃ satām /
children.translated_text: bestowing happiness, granting liberation, the essence, conferring all <s>siddhis</s> upon the virtuous.

children.text: idaṃ kavacam iṣṭaṃ ca pūjā-kāle ca yaḥ paṭhet // Jss_1,5.22 //
children.translated_text: Whoever recites this beloved protective armor at the time of worship — // Jss_1,5.22 //

children.text: hari-dāsyam avāpnoti goloke vāsam uttamam /
children.translated_text: he obtains servitude to <s>Hari</s> and supreme dwelling in <s>Goloka</s>.

children.text: ihaiva hari-bhaktiṃ ca jīvan-mukto bhaven naraḥ // Jss_1,5.23 //
children.translated_text: In this very life he obtains devotion to <s>Hari</s> and becomes liberated while living. // Jss_1,5.23 //

children.text: nārada uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: nārāyaṇarṣiṇā dattaṃ kavacaṃ yat sudurlabham /
children.translated_text: The protective armor that was given by the sage <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, so very rare —

children.text: subhadrāya brāhmaṇāya tan me vaktum ihārhasi // Jss_1,5.24 //
children.translated_text: that which was given to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Subhadrā</s> — please tell it to me now. // Jss_1,5.24 //

children.text: brahmovāca
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: mad-iṣṭa-devyāḥ kavacaṃ kathaṃ tat kathayāmi te /
children.translated_text: How shall I tell you the protective armor of my beloved deity?

children.text: mat-kaṇṭhe paśya kavacaṃ sad-ratna-guṭikānvitam // Jss_1,5.25 //
children.translated_text: Behold the protective armor on my neck, set with excellent gems. // Jss_1,5.25 //

children.text: nārāyaṇarṣiṇā dattaṃ kavacaṃ guṭikānvitam /
children.translated_text: The protective armor with its gem-amulet was given by the sage <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;

children.text: tathāpīdaṃ na kathitaṃ niṣiddhaṃ hariṇā smṛtam // Jss_1,5.26 //
children.translated_text: yet this was not narrated — it is considered forbidden by <s>Hari</s>. // Jss_1,5.26 //

children.text: tasyarṣeś ceṣṭa-devyāś ca noktaṃ tenedam īpsitam /
children.translated_text: It is the beloved deity of that sage — it was not spoken of because it is so desired.

children.text: mahyaṃ na dattā guṭikā bāndhavair bhartsitena ca // Jss_1,5.27 //
children.translated_text: The gem-amulet was not given to me, and I was rebuked by kinsmen. // Jss_1,5.27 //

children.text: ātmanaḥ kavacaṃ mantraṃ svayaṃ dātuṃ na cārhati /
children.translated_text: One's own protective armor and <s>mantra</s> one should not give away oneself;

children.text: prāṇā naṣṭāś ca dānena ceti veda-vido viduḥ // Jss_1,5.28 //
children.translated_text: life-forces are lost by giving — thus the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s> know. // Jss_1,5.28 //

children.text: śaṅkaraṃ gaccha bhagavan janmāntara-guruṃ tava /
children.translated_text: Go to <s>Śaṅkara</s>, O Blessed One — your <s>guru</s> from a previous birth.

children.text: sa eva tubhyaṃ kavacaṃ dāsyasy eva na saṃśayaḥ // Jss_1,5.29 //
children.translated_text: He alone will give you the protective armor — there is no doubt. // Jss_1,5.29 //

children.text: tvat-prāktanena viprendra sat-vareṇa śubhena ca /
children.translated_text: By your meritorious deed from a former life, O best of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, auspicious and excellent,

children.text: dhruvaṃ prāpsyasi tvaṃ vatsa kavacaṃ tat sudurlabham // Jss_1,5.30 //
children.translated_text: you will certainly obtain, O child, that protective armor, so very rare. // Jss_1,5.30 //

children.text: kumāra gaccha vaikuṇṭhaṃ sva-guruṃ paśya sat-varam /
children.translated_text: O <s>Kumāra</s>, go to <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>; see your <s>guru</s>, the excellent one.

children.text: nārāyaṇaś ca kavacaṃ tubhyaṃ dāsyasi niścitam // Jss_1,5.31 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> will certainly give you the protective armor. // Jss_1,5.31 //

children.text: sanat-kumāro bhagavān gatvā vaikuṇṭham īpsitam /
children.translated_text: The Blessed <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, having gone to the desired <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>,

children.text: saṃprāpya kavacaṃ vatsa kavacaṃ tat sudurlabham // Jss_1,5.32 //
children.translated_text: obtained the protective armor, O child — that protective armor so very rare. // Jss_1,5.32 //

children.text: ājñayā brahmaṇaś cāpi nārado gantum udyataḥ /
children.translated_text: By the command of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Nārada</s> also set out to go.

children.text: brahmā yayau brahma-lokaṃ janma-mṛtyu-jarāpaham // Jss_1,5.33 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> went to <s>Brahmaloka</s>, which removes birth, death, and old age. // Jss_1,5.33 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter of the First Night in the <s>Śrī Nārada Pañcarātra</s>, the Essence of the Nectar of Knowledge.
Sixth chapter of the First Night.

children.text: śrī-śuka uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:

children.text: sanat-kumāro vaikuṇṭhaṃ brahma-lokaṃ ca brahmaṇi ?what?/
children.translated_text: When <s>Sanatkumāra</s> went to <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> to <s>Brahmaloka</s>,

children.text: gate brahman kiṃ cakāra bhagavān nārado muniḥ // Jss_1,6.1 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Brahman</s>, what did the Blessed sage <s>Nārada</s> do? // Jss_1,6.1 //

children.text: vyāso uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Vyāsa</s> said:

children.text: munis tayoś ca gatayoḥ sa ruroda sarit-taṭe /
children.translated_text: When both of them had departed, the sage wept on the riverbank.

children.text: itas tataś ca babhrāma mad-viyoga-śucāspada // Jss_1,6.2 //
children.translated_text: He wandered here and there, an abode of grief from separation from me. // Jss_1,6.2 //

children.text: sva-mānase samālokya muni-śreṣṭhaḥ sa unmanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Contemplating within his own mind, the best of sages, his mind distracted,

children.text: dhyāyamāno hari-padaṃ śivaṃ draṣṭuṃ samutsukaḥ // Jss_1,6.3 //
children.translated_text: meditating upon the feet of <s>Hari</s>, eager to see <s>Śiva</s>, // Jss_1,6.3 //

children.text: praṇamya pitaraṃ bhaktyā kumāraṃ bhrātaraṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: having bowed with devotion to his father and to <s>Kumāra</s>, his brother,

children.text: jagāma tapasa-sthānāt kailāsābhimukhe muniḥ // Jss_1,6.4 //
children.translated_text: the sage set out from the place of austerities, headed toward <s>Kailāsa</s>. // Jss_1,6.4 //

children.text: snātvā ca kṛta-mālāyāṃ saṃpūjya parameśvaram /
children.translated_text: Having bathed in the <s>Kṛtamālā</s> river, having worshipped the Supreme Lord,

children.text: bhuktvā phalaṃ jalaṃ pītvā prayayau gandha-mādanam // Jss_1,6.5 //
children.translated_text: having eaten fruits and drunk water, he proceeded toward <s>Gandhamādana</s>. // Jss_1,6.5 //

children.text: dadarśa brāhmaṇaṃ tatra vaṭa-mūle manohare /
children.translated_text: He beheld a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> there, at the charming root of a banyan tree,

children.text: kaṭamastam dhyāyamānaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇa-caraṇāmbujam // Jss_1,6.6 //
children.translated_text: seated with downcast gaze, meditating upon the lotus feet of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, // Jss_1,6.6 //

children.text: dīrgaṃ nagnaṃ gaurāṅgaṃ dīrgha-lomabhir āvṛtam /
children.translated_text: tall, naked, fair-limbed, covered with long body-hair,

children.text: nimīlitākṣaṃ sānandaṃ sānandāśru-samanvitam // Jss_1,6.7 //
children.translated_text: with eyes closed, blissful, accompanied by tears of bliss, // Jss_1,6.7 //

children.text: pādme padmeśa-śeṣādi-sura-pūjita-vandite /
children.translated_text: upon the lotus [feet] worshipped and saluted by <s>Padmeśa</s> (Lord of <s>Padmā</s>), <s>Śeṣa</s>, and other gods —

children.text: śrī-pāda-padme śobhāḍhye śaśvat-saṃnyasta-mānasam // Jss_1,6.8 //
children.translated_text: upon those glorious <s>Śrī</s>-adorned lotus feet, his mind was perpetually fixed, // Jss_1,6.8 //

children.text: bāhya-jñāna-parityaktaṃ yoga-jñāna-viśāradam /
children.translated_text: completely devoid of external awareness, skilled in the knowledge of <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: śivasya śiṣyaṃ sad-bhaktaṃ yogīndrāṇāṃ guror guroḥ // Jss_1,6.9 //
children.translated_text: a disciple of <s>Śiva</s>, a true devotee, the <s>guru</s> of <s>gurus</s> of the kings of <s>yogins</s>. // Jss_1,6.9 //

children.text: hṛt-padme padma-nābhaṃ ca paramātmānam īśvaram /
children.translated_text: In the lotus of his heart, [he beheld] <s>Padmanābha</s> (the Lotus-naveled), the Supreme Self, the Lord,

children.text: pradīpa-kalikākāraṃ brahma-jyotiḥ-sanātanam // Jss_1,6.10 //
children.translated_text: in the form of a lamp-flame, the eternal <s>Brahma</s>-radiance, // Jss_1,6.10 //

children.text: sākṣi-svarūpaṃ paramaṃ bhagavantam adhokṣajam /
children.translated_text: the supreme Witness, the Blessed One <s>Adhokṣaja</s> (beyond the senses) —

children.text: paśyantaṃ sasmitaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ pulakāṅkita-vigraham // Jss_1,6.11 //
children.translated_text: seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> smiling, his body bristling with ecstasy. // Jss_1,6.11 //

children.text: sad-bhāvodrikta-cittaṃ ca sad-bhāvaṃ puruṣottame /
children.translated_text: His mind overflowing with true devotion, with pure feeling toward <s>Puruṣottama</s> —

children.text: dṛṣṭvā maharṣi-pravaraṃ devarṣi-vismayam yayau // Jss_1,6.12 //
children.translated_text: seeing that best of great sages, the divine sage (<s>Nārada</s>) was filled with wonder. // Jss_1,6.12 //

children.text: itas tataś ca babhrāma dadarśa svāśramaṃ muneḥ /
children.translated_text: He wandered here and there and beheld the hermitage of the sage —

children.text: atīva surahaḥ-sthānaṃ ramyaṃ ramyaṃ navaṃ navam // Jss_1,6.13 //
children.translated_text: an exceedingly beautiful, heavenly place, charming, ever fresh and new. // Jss_1,6.13 //

children.text: susnigdhaṃ sundaraṃ śuddhaṃ paraṃ svacchaṃ sarovaram /
children.translated_text: A most delightful, beautiful, pure, supremely clear lake,

children.text: śveta-raktotpala-dalaiḥ kamalaiḥ kamanīyakam // Jss_1,6.14 //
children.translated_text: lovely with petals of white and red water-lilies and lotuses, // Jss_1,6.14 //

children.text: guñjadindinda-varair ?what? makarandodarais tathā /
children.translated_text: with swarms of buzzing bees, rich with nectar,

children.text: vyākulaiḥ saṃkulaiḥ śaśvad-rājitaiś ca virājitam // Jss_1,6.15 //
children.translated_text: crowded, thronging, perpetually splendid and resplendent, // Jss_1,6.15 //

children.text: vanyair vṛkṣair bahu-vidhaiḥ phala-śākhā-suśobhitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: with many kinds of wild trees, adorned with beautiful fruits and branches —

children.text: karañjakaiś ca karajair bimbaiḥ śākhoṭikais tathā // Jss_1,6.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>karañjaka</s>, <s>karaja</s>, <s>bimba</s>, <s>śākhoṭaka</s>, // Jss_1,6.16 //

children.text: tintiḍībhiḥ kapitthaiś ca vaṭa-śiṃśapā-candanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: tamarind, wood-apple, banyan, <s>śiṃśapā</s>, sandalwood,

children.text: mandāraiḥ sindhu-vāraiś ca tāḍi-patraiḥ suśobhanaiḥ // Jss_1,6.17 //
children.translated_text: <s>mandāra</s>, <s>sindhuvāra</s>, and beautiful palm-leaves, // Jss_1,6.17 //

children.text: guvākair nāriketaiś ca kharjuraiḥ panasais tathā /
children.translated_text: areca-nut, coconut, date-palm, jackfruit,

children.text: tālaiḥ śālaiḥ piyālaiś ca hintālair vakulair api // Jss_1,6.18 //
children.translated_text: palmyra, <s>śāla</s>, <s>piyāla</s>, <s>hintāla</s>, and <s>bakula</s>, // Jss_1,6.18 //

children.text: āmrair āmrātakaiś caiva jambīrair dāḍimais tathā /
children.translated_text: mango, <s>āmrātaka</s>, citron, pomegranate,

children.text: śrī-phalair vadarībhiś ca jambubhir nāgaraṅgakaiḥ // Jss_1,6.19 //
children.translated_text: <s>śrī-phala</s>, jujube, rose-apple, and orange — // Jss_1,6.19 //

children.text: supakva-phala-śobhāḍyaiḥ susnigdhaiḥ sumanoharaiḥ /
children.translated_text: resplendent with well-ripened fruits, most delightful, most enchanting,

children.text: taruṇais taru-rājais ca nānā-jātibhir īpsitam // Jss_1,6.20 //
children.translated_text: with fresh, kingly trees of various kinds — a desired [place]. // Jss_1,6.20 //

children.text: mallikā-mālatī-kunda-ketakī-kusumaiḥ śubhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With auspicious flowers of <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine), <s>mālatī</s>, <s>kunda</s>, <s>ketakī</s> (screw-pine),

children.text: mādhavīnāṃ latā-jālaiś carcitaṃ cāru-campakaiḥ // Jss_1,6.21 //
children.translated_text: adorned with lattices of <s>mādhavī</s> creepers and lovely <s>campaka</s> blossoms, // Jss_1,6.21 //

children.text: kadambānāṃ kadambaiś ca svacchaiḥ śvetaiś ca puṣpitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: with clusters of <s>kadamba</s> flowers — clear, white, in bloom,

children.text: nāgeśvarāṇāṃ vṛndaiś ca dīptaṃ mandārakair varaiḥ // Jss_1,6.22 //
children.translated_text: with groves of <s>nāgeśvara</s> trees, blazing with excellent <s>mandāra</s> flowers, // Jss_1,6.22 //

children.text: haṃsa-kāraṇḍa-vakulaiḥ puṃs-kokila-kulais tathā /
children.translated_text: with swans, <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks, <s>bakula</s> birds, and flocks of male cuckoos —

children.text: santataṃ kūjitaṃ śuddhaṃ suvyaktaṃ sumanoharam // Jss_1,6.23 //
children.translated_text: perpetually resounding, pure, distinctly and most enchantingly, // Jss_1,6.23 //

children.text: śārdūlaiḥ śarabhaiḥ siṃhair gaṇḍakair mahiṣaiḥ param /
children.translated_text: adorned with tigers, <s>śarabhas</s>, lions, rhinoceroses, and mighty buffaloes,

children.text: manoharaiḥ kṛṣṇa-sāraiś camarabhir bhāva-bhūṣitam // Jss_1,6.24 //
children.translated_text: with enchanting black antelopes and <s>camara</s> deer — beautified by their presence, // Jss_1,6.24 //

children.text: mahā-muni-prabhāvena hiṃsā-doṣa-vivarjitam /
children.translated_text: by the power of the great sage, free from the fault of violence,

children.text: dasyu-caura-hiṃsra-jantu-bhaya-śoka-vivarjitam // Jss_1,6.25 //
children.translated_text: free from fear and sorrow of bandits, thieves, and predatory creatures, // Jss_1,6.25 //

children.text: supuṇyadaṃ tīrtha-varaṃ bhārate supraśaṃsitam /
children.translated_text: most meritorious, an excellent holy site, celebrated in <s>Bhārata</s>,

children.text: siddha-sthalaṃ siddhidaṃ taṃ mantra-siddhi-karaṃ paraṃ // Jss_1,6.26 //
children.translated_text: a place of <s>Siddhas</s>, bestowing <s>siddhis</s>, supreme for accomplishing <s>mantra</s>-<s>siddhi</s>. // Jss_1,6.26 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvāśramaṃ muni-śreṣṭho jagāma muni-saṃsadi /
children.translated_text: Having seen the hermitage, the best of sages went to the assembly of sages.

children.text: āsane ca samāsīnaṃ dhyāna-hīnaṃ dadarśa tam // Jss_1,6.27 //
children.translated_text: Seated upon a seat, devoid of meditation, he beheld him — // Jss_1,6.27 //

children.text: samuttasthau sa vegena dṛṣṭvā devarṣi-puṅgavam /
children.translated_text: he rose up with haste upon seeing the foremost of divine sages.

children.text: datvāmalaṃ phalaṃ mūlaṃ saṃbhāṣāṃ sa cakāra ha // Jss_1,6.28 //
children.translated_text: Having offered pure fruits and roots, he engaged in conversation, // Jss_1,6.28 //

children.text: praśnaṃ cakāra sa muni-vīṇā-pāṇiṃ nāradam /
children.translated_text: and questioned the sage <s>Nārada</s>, the bearer of the <s>vīṇā</s> —

children.text: sasmitaḥ sasmitaṃ śuddhaṃ śuddha-vaṃśa-samudbhavam // Jss_1,6.29 //
children.translated_text: smiling at the smiling one, pure, born of a pure lineage, // Jss_1,6.29 //

children.text: sad-bhāgyopasthitaṃ dīptaṃ jvalantaṃ brahma-tejasā /
children.translated_text: arrived by good fortune, radiant, blazing with <s>Brahma</s>-effulgence,

children.text: atithiṃ brāhmaṇa-varaṃ brahma-putraṃ ca pūjitaṃ // Jss_1,6.30 //
children.translated_text: a guest, the best of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, worthy of worship. // Jss_1,6.30 //

children.text: munir uvāca
children.translated_text: The sage said:

children.text: kiṃ nāma bhavato vipra kva yāsīti kva cāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What is your name, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>? Where are you going? From where have you come?

children.text: kva te pitā sa ko vāpi kva vāsaḥ kutra saṃbhavaḥ // Jss_1,6.31 //
children.translated_text: Where is your father? Who is he? Where is your abode? Where were you born? // Jss_1,6.31 //

children.text: māṃ vā mamāśramaṃ vāpi pūtaṃ kartum ihāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: Have you come here to purify me or my hermitage?

children.text: mūrtimad-brahma-tejo hi mama bhāgyād upasthitaḥ // Jss_1,6.32 //
children.translated_text: Embodied <s>Brahma</s>-effulgence has appeared by my good fortune! // Jss_1,6.32 //

body.translated_text: Now, the fruit of beholding a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>:

children.text: na hy ammayāni tīrthāni na devā mṛcchitāmayāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Watery holy sites do not [purify], nor do gods made of clay and metal —

children.text: te punanty urukālena vaiṣṇavo darśanena ca // Jss_1,6.33 //
children.translated_text: they purify only after a long time, but a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> purifies by mere sight. // Jss_1,6.33 //

children.text: sadyaḥ pūtāni tīrthāni sadyaḥ pūtā sa-sāgarā /
children.translated_text: Instantly purified are the holy sites; instantly purified are the oceans;

children.text: sa-śaila-kānana-dvīpā pāda-sparśād vasundharā // Jss_1,6.34 //
children.translated_text: the earth with its mountains, forests, and islands [is purified] by the touch of his feet. // Jss_1,6.34 //

children.text: dhanyo 'haṃ kṛta-kṛtyo 'haṃ saphalaṃ mama jīvanam /
children.translated_text: Blessed am I! My purpose is fulfilled! My life bears fruit!

children.text: sahasopasthito gehe brāhmaṇo vaiṣṇavo 'tithiḥ // Jss_1,6.35 //
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> guest, has suddenly appeared at my home! // Jss_1,6.35 //

children.text: pūjito vaiṣṇavo yena viśvaṃ ca tena pūjitam /
children.translated_text: By whom a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> is worshipped, by him the entire universe is worshipped.

children.text: āśramaṃ vastu-sahitaṃ sarvaṃ tubhyaṃ niveditam // Jss_1,6.36 //
children.translated_text: My hermitage with all its contents — everything is offered to you. // Jss_1,6.36 //

children.text: phalāni ca supakvāni bhuṅkṣva bhogāni sāmpratam /
children.translated_text: Eat these well-ripened fruits and enjoyments now.

children.text: suvāsitam piba svādu śītalaṃ nirmalaṃ jalam // Jss_1,6.37 //
children.translated_text: Drink this fragrant, sweet, cool, pure water. // Jss_1,6.37 //

children.text: dugdhaṃ ca surabhī-dattaṃ ramyaṃ madhuritaṃ madhu /
children.translated_text: Milk given by the divine cow (<s>Surabhī</s>), delightful, sweetened with honey,

children.text: paripakvaṃ phala-rasaṃ piba svādu muhur muhuḥ // Jss_1,6.38 //
children.translated_text: and well-ripened fruit-juice — drink the sweet nectar again and again! // Jss_1,6.38 //

children.text: sukha-bījye sutalpe ca śayanaṃ kuru sundare /
children.translated_text: Upon a comfortable, fine bed, take rest, O beautiful one,

children.text: suśīta-vāta-saugandhya-pūtena surabhī-kṛte // Jss_1,6.39 //
children.translated_text: purified by the cool, fragrant, sweet breeze. // Jss_1,6.39 //

body.translated_text: Now, the fruit of worshipping a guest:

children.text: atithir yasya puṣṭo hi tasya puṣṭo hariḥ svayam /
children.translated_text: 'He whose guest is nourished — for him <s>Hari</s> Himself is nourished.

children.text: harau tuṣṭe gurus tuṣṭo gurau tuṣṭe jagat-trayam // Jss_1,6.40 //
children.translated_text: When <s>Hari</s> is pleased, the <s>guru</s> is pleased; when the <s>guru</s> is pleased, the three worlds [are pleased]. // Jss_1,6.40 //

children.text: adhiṣṭhātātithir gehe santataṃ sarva-devatāḥ /
children.translated_text: A guest presiding in the home — perpetually [represents] all the deities,

children.text: tīrthāny etāni sarvāṇi puṇyāni ca vratāni ca // Jss_1,6.41 //
children.translated_text: all these holy sites, meritorious deeds, and vows, // Jss_1,6.41 //

children.text: tapāṃsi yajñāḥ satyaṃ ca śīlaṃ dharmaḥ sukarma ca /
children.translated_text: austerities, sacrifices, truthfulness, good conduct, <s>dharma</s>, and virtuous deeds —

children.text: apūjitair atithibhir sārdhaṃ sarve prayānti te // Jss_1,6.42 //
children.translated_text: all these depart along with guests who are not worshipped. // Jss_1,6.42 //

children.text: athātithi-vimukhe doṣāḥ
children.translated_text: Now, the faults of one who turns away a guest:

children.text: atithir yasya bhagnāśo gṛhāt pratinivartate /
children.translated_text: 'The guest whose hopes are dashed and who turns away from the home —

children.text: pitaras tasya devāś ca puṇyaṃ dharma-vratāśanāḥ // Jss_1,6.43 //
children.translated_text: the ancestors of that person, the gods, his merit, <s>dharma</s>, vows, and nourishment, // Jss_1,6.43 //

children.text: yamaḥ pratiṣṭhā lakṣmīś cābhīṣṭa-devo gurus tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> (Death), prosperity, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, his cherished deity, and his <s>guru</s> likewise —

children.text: nirāśāḥ pratigacchanti tyaktvā pāpaṃ ca pūruṣam // Jss_1,6.44 //
children.translated_text: they depart hopeless, having abandoned sinful men. // Jss 1.6.44 //

children.text: strī-ghnaiś caiva kṛta-ghnaiś ca brahma-ghnair guru-talpa-gaiḥ /
children.translated_text: By those who kill women, by the ungrateful, by slayers of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, by those who defile the guru's bed,

children.text: viśvāsa-ghātibhir duṣṭair mitra-drohibhir eva ca // Jss_1,6.45 //
children.translated_text: by treacherous betrayers, by the wicked, and by those who harm their friends — // Jss 1.6.45 //

children.text: satya-ghnaiś ca kṛta-ghnaiś ca pāpibhiḥ sthāpibhis tathā /
children.translated_text: by destroyers of truth, by the ungrateful, by sinners, by those who cause miscarriage,

children.text: dānāpahāribhiś caiva kanyā-vikriyibhis tathā // Jss_1,6.46 //
children.translated_text: by those who steal gifts, and by those who sell their daughters — // Jss 1.6.46 //

children.text: sīmāpahāribhiś caiva mithyā-sākṣi-pradātṛbhiḥ /
children.translated_text: by those who steal boundary lands, by those who give false testimony,

children.text: brahma-svahāribhiś caiva tathā sthāpyasvahāribhiḥ // Jss_1,6.47 //
children.translated_text: by those who steal the property of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and likewise by those who steal endowed property — // Jss 1.6.47 //

children.text: vṛṣa-vāhair devalaiś ca tathaiva grāma-yājibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: by those who ride bulls, by temple-priests [who sell religion], and by those who serve as village-priests,

children.text: śūdrānna-bhojibhiś caiva śūdra-śrāddhāha-bhojibhiḥ // Jss_1,6.48 //
children.translated_text: by those who eat the food of <s>Śūdras</s>, and by those who eat at <s>Śūdra</s> funeral feasts — // Jss 1.6.48 //

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa-vimukhair viprair hiṃsrair nara-vighātibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who are hostile to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, by violent men who harm others,

children.text: gurāv abhaktai rogārtaiḥ śaśvan-mithyā-pravādibhiḥ // Jss_1,6.49 //
