children.translated_text: by those disloyal to their <s>Guru</s>, by those afflicted with disease, and by those who constantly speak falsehood — // Jss 1.6.49 //

children.text: vipra-strī-gāmibhiḥ śūdrair mātṛ-gāmibhir eva ca /
children.translated_text: by <s>Śūdras</s> who approach <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> women, and by those who approach their own mothers,

children.text: aśvattha-ghātibhiś caiva patnībhiḥ pati-ghātibhiḥ // Jss_1,6.50 //
children.translated_text: by those who cut down the <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig tree), and by wives who kill their husbands — // Jss 1.6.50 //

children.text: pitṛ-mātṛ-ghātibhiś ca śaraṇāgata-ghātibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: by those who kill their fathers and mothers, and by those who kill those who have sought refuge,

children.text: brāhmaṇa-kṣatra-viṭ-śūdraiḥ śilā-svarṇāpahāribhiḥ // Jss_1,6.51 //
children.translated_text: by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s> who steal stone and gold — // Jss 1.6.51 //

body.text: tulyo bhavati viprendrātithir eva tv anarcitaḥ /
body.translated_text: one becomes equal [in sin] to them, O chief of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, if a guest is left unhonored.

children.text: itya evam uktvā muniḥ pūjayām āsa nāradam /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the sage worshipped <s>Nārada</s>,

children.text: miṣṭaṃ ca bhojayām āsa śāyayām āsa bhaktitaḥ // Jss_1,6.52 //
children.translated_text: fed him delicious food, and laid him to rest with devotion. // Jss 1.6.52 //

children.text: śrī-nārada uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Nārada</s> said:

children.text: nārado 'haṃ muni-śreṣṭha brāhmaṇo brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ /
children.translated_text: I am <s>Nārada</s>, O best of sages, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>;

children.text: tapaḥ-sthalād āgato 'haṃ yāmi kailāsam īpsitam // Jss_1,6.53 //
children.translated_text: I have come from a place of austerity, and I am going to the desired <s>Kailāsa</s>. // Jss 1.6.53 //

children.text: ātmānaṃ pāvanaṃ kartuṃ tvāṃ ca draṣṭum ihāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: I have come here to purify myself and to see you;

children.text: punanti prāṇinaḥ sarve viṣṇu-bhakta-pradarśanāt // Jss_1,6.54 //
children.translated_text: all beings are purified by the sight of a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // Jss 1.6.54 //

children.text: ko bhavān dhyāna-pūtaś ca nagnaś ca kaṭa-mastakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who are you, purified by meditation, naked, with a mat upon your head?

children.text: kiṃ dhyāyase mahā-bhāga śreṣṭha-devaś ca ko guruh // Jss_1,6.55 //
children.translated_text: What do you meditate upon, O fortunate one? And who is your supreme deity and <s>Guru</s>? // Jss 1.6.55 //

children.text: munir uvāca
children.translated_text: The sage said:

children.text: jīva-mukto bhavān eva punāsi bhuvana-trayam /
children.translated_text: You yourself are indeed a <s>jīvanmukta</s> (one liberated while living), and you purify the three worlds.

children.text: yasya tatra kule janma tasya tat-tad-vacomanaḥ // Jss_1,6.56 //
children.translated_text: In whichever family one is born, one's speech and mind correspond to that. // Jss 1.6.56 //

children.text: putre yaśasi toye ca kavitvena ca vidyayā /
children.translated_text: Through one's son, fame, waters, poetic skill, and learning,

children.text: pratiśhṭhāyāṃ ca jñāyeta sarveṣāṃ mānasaṃ nṛṇām // Jss_1,6.57 //
children.translated_text: and through one's reputation, the minds of all men are known. // Jss 1.6.57 //

children.text: vidhātā jagatāṃ brahmā brahmaikatāna-mānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: The creator of the worlds is <s>Brahmā</s>, whose mind is fixed single-pointedly on <s>Brahman</s>;

children.text: tat-putro 'si mahākhyāto devarṣi-pravaro mahān // Jss_1,6.58 //
children.translated_text: you are his son, widely renowned, the foremost and great among divine sages. // Jss 1.6.58 //

children.text: lomaśo ' haṃ mahā-bhāga jagat-pāvana-pāvana /
children.translated_text: I am <s>Lomaśa</s>, O fortunate one, O purifier of the world's purifiers!

children.text: nagno'lpāyur vivekī ca vāsasā kiṃ prayojanam // Jss_1,6.59 //
children.translated_text: I am naked, short-lived, and discerning — what use is clothing? // Jss 1.6.59 //

children.text: vṛkṣa-mūle nivāse me chatreṇa kiṃ gṛheṇa ca /
children.translated_text: My dwelling is at the root of a tree — what use is an umbrella or a house?

children.text: raudra-vṛṣṭi-vāraṇārthaṃ sāṃprataṃ kaṭa-mastakaḥ // Jss_1,6.60 //
children.translated_text: For warding off fierce rain, I presently have a mat upon my head. // Jss 1.6.60 //

children.text: jala-budbuda-vidyudvat-trailokyaṃ kṛtrimaṃ dvija /
children.translated_text: The three worlds are artificial, like a water-bubble or lightning, O twice-born;

children.text: brahmādi-tṛṇa-paryantaṃ sarvaṃ mithyāiva svapnavat // Jss_1,6.61 //
children.translated_text: from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, everything is false, like a dream. // Jss 1.6.61 //

children.text: kiṃ kalatreṇa putreṇa dhanena saṃpadā śriyā /
children.translated_text: What use is a wife, a son, wealth, prosperity, or fortune?

children.text: kiṃ vittena ca rūpeṇa jīvanālpāyuṣā mune // Jss_1,6.62 //
children.translated_text: What use is money or beauty for one whose life is short-lived, O sage? // Jss 1.6.62 //

children.text: indrasya patanenaiva lomakotpāṭanaṃ mama /
children.translated_text: With each fall of <s>Indra</s>, one hair falls from my body;

children.text: manoś ca patanaṃ tatra māyayā kiṃ prayojanam // Jss_1,6.63 //
children.translated_text: with the fall of each <s>Manu</s>, what use is illusion (<s>māyā</s>) there? // Jss 1.6.63 //

children.text: sarva-lomakotpāṭanena keśaughotpāṭanena ca /
children.translated_text: When all the body-hairs have fallen and the head-hair has been plucked out,

children.text: alpāyuṣo mama mune maraṇaṃ niścitaṃ bhavet // Jss_1,6.64 //
children.translated_text: death is certain for me, short-lived as I am, O sage. // Jss 1.6.64 //

children.text: dhyāye śrī-pāda-padmaṃ tat-pādma-padmeśa-vanditam /
children.translated_text: I meditate upon the blessed lotus feet, worshipped by <s>Padma</s> (Lakṣmī) and <s>Padmeśa</s> (Brahmā),

children.text: parasya prakṛtes tasya kṛṣṇasya paramātmanaḥ // Jss_1,6.65 //
children.translated_text: of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Self, who is beyond <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). // Jss 1.6.65 //

children.text: tasya me 'bhīṣṭa-devasya sarveṣāṃ kāraṇasya ca /
children.translated_text: Of that my chosen deity, the cause of all,

children.text: gurur me jagatāṃ nātho yogīndrāṇāṃ guruḥ śivaḥ // Jss_1,6.66 //
children.translated_text: my <s>Guru</s> is <s>Śiva</s>, the lord of the worlds, the Guru of the lords of <s>yogins</s>. // Jss 1.6.66 //

children.text: mat-kaṇṭhe kavacaṃ yasya mad-guruḥ kathayiṣyati /
children.translated_text: Whose protective mantra-armor is upon my neck — that my <s>Guru</s> shall reveal;

children.text: guror niṣedho yatrāste tad vaktuṃ kaḥ kṣamo bhuvi // Jss_1,6.67 //
children.translated_text: where the prohibition of the <s>Guru</s> exists, who on earth is capable of speaking it? // Jss 1.6.67 //

children.text: guroś ca vacanaṃ yo hi pālanaṃ na karoti ca /
children.translated_text: He who does not obey the words of the <s>Guru</s>,

children.text: gurūktam uktvā pāpī sa brahma-hatyāṃ labhed dhruvam // Jss_1,6.68 //
children.translated_text: that sinner, having spoken what the <s>Guru</s> forbade, surely incurs the sin of <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a Brāhmaṇa). // Jss 1.6.68 //

children.text: sva-guruṃ śiva-rūpaṃ ca tad-bhinnaṃ manyate hi yaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who considers his own <s>Guru</s>, who is of the form of <s>Śiva</s>, as different [from Śiva] —

children.text: brahma-hatyāṃ labhet so 'pi vighnas tasya pade pade // Jss_1,6.69 //
children.translated_text: he too incurs <s>brahmahatyā</s>, and obstacles beset him at every step. // Jss 1.6.69 //

children.text: akartavyaṃ tu kartavyaṃ pālanīyaṃ guror vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even what ought not to be done must be done — the word of the <s>Guru</s> must be obeyed;

children.text: apālane sarva-vighnaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ // Jss_1,6.70 //
children.translated_text: in disobedience, one obtains every obstacle — there is no doubt in this. // Jss 1.6.70 //

children.text: āśiṣā pāda-rajasā cocchiṣṭāliṅgena ca /
children.translated_text: By his blessing, by the dust of his feet, and by the embrace of his leftovers,

children.text: mucyate sarva-pāpebhyo jīvan-mukto bhaven naraḥ // Jss_1,6.71 //
children.translated_text: one is freed from all sins and becomes a <s>jīvanmukta</s> (liberated while living). // Jss 1.6.71 //

children.text: sva-guruṃ śaṅkaraṃ paśya gaccha kailāsam īpsitam /
children.translated_text: See your own <s>Guru</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva), and go to the desired <s>Kailāsa</s>!

children.text: mucyate vighna-pāpebhyo guroś caraṇa-darśanāt // Jss_1,6.72 //
children.translated_text: One is freed from obstacles and sins by the sight of the <s>Guru's</s> feet. // Jss 1.6.72 //

body.text:
iti śrī-nārada-pañca-rātre jñānāmṛta-sāre prathmaika-rātre
lomaśa-nārada-saṃvāde ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth chapter, the dialogue between <s>Lomaśa</s> and <s>Nārada</s>, in the first night of the <s>Śrī Nārada Pañcarātra</s>, [known as] the <s>Jñānāmṛtasāra</s>.
Seventh chapter of the first night.

children.text: saṃbhāṣya lomaśaṃ tasmāj jagāma nārado muniḥ /
children.translated_text: Having conversed with <s>Lomaśa</s>, the sage <s>Nārada</s> departed from there

children.text: puṣpa-bhadrā-nadī-tīram atīva sumanoharam // Jss_1,7.1 //
children.translated_text: to the bank of the <s>Puṣpabhadrā</s> river, exceedingly beautiful. // Jss 1.7.1 //

children.text: yatrāste śṛṅga-kūṭaś ca śuddha-sphaṭika-sannibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Where stands <s>Śṛṅgakūṭa</s>, with [peaks] resembling pure crystal,

children.text: nānā-vṛkṣa-samāyuktais tribhir anyaiḥ sarovaraiḥ // Jss_1,7.2 //
children.translated_text: endowed with various trees, and with three other lakes — // Jss 1.7.2 //

children.text: haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇair bhramarair dhvani-sundaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: teeming with swans and <s>kāraṇḍava</s> birds, with bees making sweet sounds,

children.text: puṃs-kokila-ninādaiś ca santataṃ sumanoharaiḥ // Jss_1,7.3 //
children.translated_text: and with the constantly enchanting calls of male cuckoos. // Jss 1.7.3 //

children.text: śaitya-saugandhya-māndhyaiś ca vāyubhiḥ surabhī-kṛtaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Made fragrant by breezes that are cool, sweet-smelling, and gentle,

children.text: samādhi-yukto yatrāste mārkaṇḍeyo mahā-muniḥ // Jss_1,7.4 //
children.translated_text: where the great sage <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> abides, absorbed in <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption). // Jss 1.7.4 //

children.text: sa munir nāradaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaktyā ca praṇanāma ca /
children.translated_text: That sage, seeing <s>Nārada</s>, bowed to him with devotion

children.text: papraccha kuśalaṃ śāntaṃ śāntaḥ sattva-guṇāśrayaḥ // Jss_1,7.5 //
children.translated_text: and asked about his welfare peacefully, being himself peaceful and established in <s>sattva-guṇa</s>. // Jss 1.7.5 //

children.text: mārkaṇḍeyo uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:

children.text: adya me saphalaṃ janma jīvanaṃ cātisārthakam /
children.translated_text: Today my birth has become fruitful and my life supremely meaningful,

children.text: mamāśrame puṇya-rāśir brahma-putraś ca nāradaḥ // Jss_1,7.6 //
children.translated_text: for <s>Nārada</s>, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, a treasury of merit, is in my <s>āśrama</s>. // Jss 1.7.6 //

children.text: aho devarṣi-pravaro dīptamān brahma-tejasā /
children.translated_text: Ah, the foremost of divine sages, radiant with the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>!

children.text: kva yāsi kuta āyāsi kiṃ te manasi vartate // Jss_1,7.7 //
children.translated_text: Where are you going? From where have you come? What is in your mind? // Jss 1.7.7 //

children.text: mānasaṃ prāṇinām eva sarva-karmaika-kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: The mind of beings is indeed the sole cause of all actions;

children.text: manonurūpaṃ vākyaṃ ca vākyena prasphuṭaṃ manaḥ // Jss_1,7.8 //
children.translated_text: speech conforms to the mind, and through speech the mind is revealed. // Jss 1.7.8 //

children.text: muneś ca vacanaṃ śrutvā vīṇā-pāṇi svam īpsitam /
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of the sage, <s>Nārada</s>, the <s>vīṇā</s>-bearer, [spoke] his desired [words];

children.text: uvāca sasmitaṃ śāntaṃ vacaḥ satyaṃ sudhopamam // Jss_1,7.9 //
children.translated_text: he spoke peaceful, truthful words, like <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), with a smile. // Jss 1.7.9 //

children.text: nārada uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: he bandho yāmi kailāsaṃ jñānārthaṃ jñānināṃ varam /
children.translated_text: O friend, I am going to <s>Kailāsa</s>, for the sake of knowledge, to [see] the best among the wise,

children.text: draṣṭuṃ mahā-devaṃ ca praṇāmaṃ kartum īśvaram // Jss_1,7.10 //
children.translated_text: to behold <s>Mahādeva</s> and to offer obeisance to the Lord. // Jss 1.7.10 //

children.text: pūjāṃ gṛhītvā cety uktvā prayayau nārado muniḥ /
children.translated_text: Having received worship and having spoken thus, the sage <s>Nārada</s> departed;

children.text: mārkaṇḍeyaś ca śokārtaḥ sadvicchedaḥ sudāruṇaḥ // Jss_1,7.11 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> was stricken with grief, for separation from the virtuous is exceedingly painful. // Jss 1.7.11 //

children.text: himālayaṃ ca durlaghyaṃ vilaghyaṃ caiva līlayā /
children.translated_text: The <s>Himālaya</s>, difficult to cross, he crossed effortlessly, as if in play;

children.text: svarga-mandākinī-tīraṃ kailāsaṃ prayayau muniḥ // Jss_1,7.12 //
children.translated_text: the sage proceeded to <s>Kailāsa</s>, on the banks of the celestial <s>Mandākinī</s>. // Jss 1.7.12 //

children.text: dadarśa vaṭa-vṛkṣaṃ ca yojanāyatam ucchritam /
children.translated_text: He saw a banyan tree, a <s>yojana</s> wide and tall,

children.text: śobhitaṃ śatakaiḥ skandhaiḥ rakta-pakva-phalānvitaiḥ // Jss_1,7.13 //
children.translated_text: adorned with hundreds of branches bearing ripe red fruits — // Jss 1.7.13 //

children.text: susnigdhaiḥ sundaraiḥ ramyai ramya-pakṣīndra-saṃkulaiḥ /
children.translated_text: smooth, beautiful, and delightful, filled with splendid birds,

children.text: siddhendraiś ca munīndraiś yogīndraiḥ pariśobhitam // Jss_1,7.14 //
children.translated_text: graced by lords of <s>Siddhas</s>, lords of sages, and lords of <s>yogins</s>. // Jss 1.7.14 //

children.text: praṇatāṃs tāṃś ca saṃbhāṣya pārvatī-kānanaṃ yayau /
children.translated_text: Having greeted and conversed with them who bowed to him, he went to the garden of <s>Pārvatī</s>,

children.text: sundaraṃ vartulākāraṃ catur-yojanam īpsitam // Jss_1,7.15 //
children.translated_text: beautiful, circular in shape, four <s>yojanas</s> in extent, and most desired — // Jss 1.7.15 //

children.text: śobhitaṃ sundarai ramyaiḥ saptabhiś ca sarovaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: adorned with seven beautiful and delightful lakes,

children.text: śaśvan-madhukarāsakta-padma-rāji-virājitaiḥ // Jss_1,7.16 //
children.translated_text: resplendent with rows of lotuses to which bees were perpetually attached — // Jss 1.7.16 //

children.text: nīla-raktotpala-dala-paṭalaiḥ pariśobhitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: adorned with clusters of blue and red lotus petals,

children.text: puṣpodyānaiś ca śatakaiḥ puṣpitaiḥ sumanoharaiḥ // Jss_1,7.17 //
children.translated_text: and with hundreds of blooming, enchanting flower gardens — // Jss 1.7.17 //

children.text: mallikā-mālatī-kunda-yūthikā-mādhavī-latā /
children.translated_text: <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine), <s>mālatī</s>, <s>kunda</s>, <s>yūthikā</s>, <s>mādhavī</s> creepers,

children.text: ketakī-campakāśoka-mandāraka-virājikā // Jss_1,7.18 //
children.translated_text: <s>ketakī</s> (screwpine), <s>campaka</s>, <s>aśoka</s>, and <s>mandāraka</s> (coral tree), splendidly arrayed — // Jss 1.7.18 //

children.text: nāga-punnāga-kuṭajapāṭalājñiṇṭjñijjñikā /
children.translated_text: <s>nāga</s> (Mesua), <s>punnāga</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>pāṭalā</s>, and other flowering [plants],

children.text: viṣṇu-krāntā ca tulasī śophalī saptalā tathā // Jss_1,7.19 //
children.translated_text: <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s> (butterfly pea), <s>tulasī</s> (sacred basil), <s>śephalī</s> (night jasmine), and <s>saptalā</s> likewise — // Jss 1.7.19 //

children.text: eteṣāṃ ca samūhaiś ca puṣpa-vallī-virājitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: with clusters of all these, resplendent with flowering vines,

children.text: āmrair āmrātakais tālanārikelaiḥ piyālakaiḥ // Jss_1,7.20 //
children.translated_text: with mango trees, <s>āmrātaka</s> (hog plum), palm trees, coconut palms, and <s>piyāla</s> (buchanania) trees — // Jss 1.7.20 //

children.text: kharjūraiś ca guvākaiś ca palāsair jambubhis tathā /
children.translated_text: with date palms, betel-nut palms, <s>palāśa</s> (flame of the forest), <s>jambu</s> (rose apple),

children.text: dāḍimbaiś cāpi jambīrair nimbaiś caiva vaṭais tathā // Jss_1,7.21 //
children.translated_text: pomegranates, citrons, neem trees, and banyan trees — // Jss 1.7.21 //

children.text: karañjair vadarībhiś ca paritaḥ śrī-phalojjvalaiḥ /
children.translated_text: with <s>karañja</s> (pongamia) and <s>badarī</s> (jujube), surrounded by trees gleaming with <s>śrīphala</s> (bilva) fruits,

children.text: kadambānāṃ kadambaiś ca tintiṇḍīnāṃ kadambakaiḥ // Jss_1,7.22 //
children.translated_text: with clusters of <s>kadamba</s> trees and groves of <s>tintiṇḍī</s> (tamarind) — // Jss 1.7.22 //

children.text: aśvatthaiḥ saralaiḥ śālaiḥ śālmalīnāṃ samūhakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: with <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), <s>sarala</s> (pine), <s>śāla</s> (sal), and clusters of <s>śālmalī</s> (silk-cotton) trees,

children.text: vaṭa-śākhoṭakaiḥ kundaiḥ śaṃgubhiḥ sapta-parṇakaiḥ // Jss_1,7.23 //
children.translated_text: with banyan offshoots and <s>śākhoṭaka</s> trees, <s>kunda</s>, <s>śaṅgu</s> (arjuna), and <s>saptaparṇa</s> (devil tree) — // Jss 1.7.23 //

children.text: picchilaiḥ parṇa-śālaiś ca gambhāribhiś ca valgukaiḥ /
children.translated_text: with <s>picchila</s> trees, leaf-halls, and graceful <s>gambhārī</s> (gmelina) trees,

children.text: hiṅgulair añjanair valkair bhūrja-patraiḥ sapatrakaiḥ // Jss_1,7.24 //
children.translated_text: with <s>hiṅgula</s> (vermilion) trees, <s>añjana</s>, bark-trees, and birch-bark with their leaves — // Jss 1.7.24 //

children.text: anyaiś ca durlabhair vanyaiḥ puṣpa-patrair virājitam /
children.translated_text: and adorned with other rare forest trees with flowers and leaves,

children.text: kalpa-vṛkṣaiḥ pārijātaiś cāru-candana-pallavaiḥ // Jss_1,7.25 //
children.translated_text: with wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpa-vṛkṣas</s>), <s>pārijāta</s> trees, and beautiful sandalwood sprouts — // Jss 1.7.25 //

children.text: susnigdha-sthala-padmaiś ca citritair bhūmi-campakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: with smooth land-lotuses and colorful ground-<s>campaka</s> flowers,

children.text: anyaiś ca durlabhair vanyaiḥ puṣpa-patrair vibhūṣitam // Jss_1,7.26 //
children.translated_text: and embellished with other rare forest trees with flowers and leaves. // Jss 1.7.26 //

children.text: siṃhendraiḥ śarabhendraiś ca gajendrair gaṇḍakendraiḥ /
children.translated_text: With lords of lions, lords of <s>śarabhas</s> (eight-legged beasts), lords of elephants, and lords of rhinoceroses,

children.text: śārdūlendraiś ca mahiṣair aśvaiś ca vanya-śūkaraiḥ // Jss_1,7.27 //
children.translated_text: with lords of tigers, buffaloes, horses, and wild boars — // Jss 1.7.27 //

body.text:
śallakair ballakair markaiḥ kūṭaiś ca śaśakaiḥ śakaiḥ /
kṛṣṇa-sāraiś ca hariṇaiś camarī-cāmarojjvalam // Jss_1,7./28 //
body.translated_text: with porcupines, bears, monkeys, wolves, hares, and deer, with black antelope and spotted deer, and resplendent with <s>camarī</s> yaks and <s>cāmara</s> fans — // Jss 1.7.28 //

children.text: puṃs-kokola-kulānāṃ ca gānaiś ca virājitam /
children.translated_text: resplendent with the songs of flocks of male cuckoos,

children.text: mattānāṃ pallava-sthānāṃ mādhaveṣu manoharam // Jss_1,7.29 //
children.translated_text: enchanting with intoxicated [birds] perched on tender shoots among the <s>mādhavī</s> creepers — // Jss 1.7.29 //

children.text: śukānāṃ rāja-haṃsānāṃ mayūrāṇāṃ ca putrakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: with the young of parrots, royal swans, and peacocks,

children.text: kṣema-karī-khañjanānāṃ rājibhiś ca manoharam // Jss_1,7.30 //
children.translated_text: enchanting with flocks of <s>kṣemakarī</s> birds and wagtails — // Jss 1.7.30 //

children.text: harit-pīta-rakta-kṛṣṇa-supakva-phala-patrakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: with green, yellow, red, and black well-ripened fruits and leaves,

children.text: susnigdhākṣata-patraiś ca nūtanair abhibhūṣitam // Jss_1,7.31 //
children.translated_text: adorned with fresh, smooth, and unblemished foliage. // Jss 1.7.31 //

children.text: hiṃsā-bhayādi-rahitaṃ sarveṣāṃ paśu-pakṣiṇāṃ /
children.translated_text: Free from the fear of violence for all animals and birds,

children.text: parasparaṃ ca suprītaṃ hiṃsrāṇāṃ kṣudra-jantubhiḥ // Jss_1,7.32 //
children.translated_text: all being mutually friendly, even the predatory ones with small creatures. // Jss 1.7.32 //

children.text: tatra krīḍā-sthalaṃ ramyaṃ pārvatī-parameśayoḥ /
children.translated_text: There is the delightful pleasure-ground of <s>Pārvatī</s> and <s>Parameśvara</s>,

children.text: munīndrair indra-nīlaiś ca padma-rāgaiḥ pariṣkṛtam // Jss_1,7.33 //
children.translated_text: adorned with sapphires (<s>indranīla</s>) and rubies (<s>padmarāga</s>) by lords of sages. // Jss 1.7.33 //

children.text: krośāyataṃ parimitaṃ vartulaṃ candra-vimbavat /
children.translated_text: It is a <s>krośa</s> (two miles) in extent, measured and circular like the orb of the moon,

children.text: amlāna-rambhā-stambhānāṃ lakṣa-lakṣaiś ca veṣṭitam // Jss_1,7.34 //
children.translated_text: surrounded by hundreds of thousands of unfading plantain pillars. // Jss 1.7.34 //

children.text: citritaṃ sūkṣma-sūtrāktair nūtanair abhibhūṣitam /
children.translated_text: Decorated with fine thread-work, embellished with fresh [ornaments],

children.text: nūtanākṣata-patraiś ca lalitaiḥ pariśobhitam // Jss_1,7.35 //
children.translated_text: and graced with elegant, fresh, and unblemished leaf-decorations. // Jss 1.7.35 //

children.text: rakta-pītāsitaiḥ snigdhair amlānaiḥ sumanoharaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With red, yellow, and dark, smooth, unfading, and enchanting [garlands],

children.text: paritaḥ paritaḥ śaśvan mālājālair vibhūṣitam // Jss_1,7.36 //
children.translated_text: adorned on every side perpetually with nets of garlands. // Jss 1.7.36 //

children.text: śayyā-bhūtaṃ sutalpaiś ca snigdha-campaka-candanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The ground serves as a bed, with smooth couches of <s>campaka</s> and sandalwood,

children.text: puṣpa-candana-yuktena vāyunā surabhī-kṛtam // Jss_1,7.37 //
children.translated_text: made fragrant by breezes carrying flowers and sandalwood. // Jss 1.7.37 //

children.text: kastūrī-kuṅkamāsakta-sugandhi-candanaiḥ sitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With white and fragrant sandalwood paste mixed with musk and saffron,

children.text: mārjitaṃ citritaṃ citraiḥ parito raṅga-vastubhiḥ // Jss_1,7.38 //
children.translated_text: polished and decorated all around with colorful dyes and pigments. // Jss 1.7.38 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tad adbhutaṃ śīghraṃ prayayau svar-ṇadīṃ muniḥ /
children.translated_text: Having seen that wondrous [place], the sage quickly proceeded to the celestial river,

children.text: śuddha-sphaṭika-saṃkāsāṃ sarva-pāpa-vināśinīm // Jss_1,7.39 //
children.translated_text: resembling pure crystal, the destroyer of all sins — // Jss 1.7.39 //

children.text: bhavābdhighora-taraṇe taraṇīṃ nityanūtanām /
children.translated_text: the vessel for crossing the terrible ocean of worldly existence, ever fresh,

children.text: kṛṣṇa-pāda-prasūtāṃ ca jagat-pūjyāṃ pati-vratāṃ // Jss_1,7.40 //
children.translated_text: born from the feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, worshipped by the world, devoted to her lord — // Jss 1.7.40 //

children.text: snāṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ ca saṃpūjya paramātmānam īśvaram /
children.translated_text: having bathed and worshipped <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Self, the Lord —

children.text: prakṛteḥ parimiṣṭaṃ ca nirliptaṃ nirguṇaṃ param // Jss_1,7.41 //
children.translated_text: separated from <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), untainted, beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), supreme, // 1.7.41 //

children.text: sākṣiṇaṃ karmaṇām eva brahma jyotiḥ sanātanam /
children.translated_text: the witness of all actions, <s>Brahman</s>, the eternal light —

children.text: prayayau purato ramyaṃ rāja-mārgaṃ dadarśa saḥ // Jss_1,7.42 //
children.translated_text: he went forward and beheld a beautiful royal highway. // 1.7.42 //

children.text: maṇibhiḥ sphaṭikākārair amalair bahu-mūlyakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With gems of crystal-like appearance, pure and of great value,

children.text: pariṣkṛtaṃ ca sarvatra nirmitaṃ viśva-karmaṇā // Jss_1,7.43 //
children.translated_text: adorned everywhere, fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>, // 1.7.43 //

children.text: satāṃ puṇyavatāṃ dṛṣṭam adṛṣṭaṃ kṛta-pāpinām /
children.translated_text: visible to the virtuous and meritorious, invisible to sinners,

children.text: dhanuḥ śataṃ parimitaṃ citra-rāji-virājitam // Jss_1,7.44 //
children.translated_text: measuring a hundred bow-lengths, resplendent with rows of paintings, // 1.7.44 //

children.text: dadhyaṃ sarvāśramāntaṃ ca prakhyāt koṭi-guṇottaram /
children.translated_text: extending to the boundary of all the hermitages, renowned, ten million times superior,

children.text: rathaṃ dadarśa purato manoyāyi manoharam // Jss_1,7.45 //
children.translated_text: he beheld before him a chariot, swift as thought, enchanting, // 1.7.45 //

children.text: amūlya-ratna-nirmāṇa-vimāṇa-sāra-sundaram /
children.translated_text: beautiful in its essential construction of priceless gems like a celestial vehicle,

children.text: dhanur lakṣaṃ parimitaṃ parito vartulākṛtam // Jss_1,7.46 //
children.translated_text: measuring a hundred thousand bow-lengths in circumference, circular in shape, // 1.7.46 //

children.text: ūrdhva-sthitam ūrdhva-gaṃ ca sahasra-cakra-saṃyutam /
children.translated_text: positioned above, moving upward, equipped with a thousand wheels,

children.text: dhanur lakṣo 'pi sūtaṃ ca vahni-śuddhāṃśukānvitam // Jss_1,7.47 //
children.translated_text: the charioteer too measuring a hundred thousand bow-lengths, clad in fire-purified garments, // 1.7.47 //

children.text: hīrāsāra-vinirmāṇaṃ sucāru-kalaśojjvalam /
children.translated_text: constructed of the essence of diamonds, brilliant with beautiful pinnacles,

children.text: ratna-pradīpa-dīptāḍhyaṃ ratna-darpaṇa-bhūṣitam // Jss_1,7.48 //
children.translated_text: rich with blazing gem-lamps, adorned with gem-mirrors, // 1.7.48 //

children.text: muktāśukti-nibaddhaiś ca śobhitaṃ śveta-cāmaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: beautified with white <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks) fastened with pearl-oyster shells,

children.text: māṇikya-sāra-hāreṇa maṇi-rājair virājitam // Jss_1,7.49 //
children.translated_text: resplendent with ruby-essence garlands and the best of gems, // 1.7.49 //

children.text: pārijāṭa-prasūtānāṃ māyājālaiḥ pariṣkṛtam /
children.translated_text: embellished with magical arrays of flowers born from the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree,

children.text: grīṣma-madhyāhna-mārtaṇḍaṃ sahasra-sadṛśojjvalam // Jss_1,7.50 //
children.translated_text: blazing like a thousand midsummer midday suns, // 1.7.50 //

children.text: īśvarecchā-vinirmāṇaṃ kāma-puraṃ ca kāminām /
children.translated_text: fashioned by the will of the Lord, the city of desire for lovers,

children.text: sarva-bhoga-samāviṣṭaṃ kalpa-vṛkṣa-paraṃ varam // Jss_1,7.51 //
children.translated_text: filled with every enjoyment, supreme beyond the wish-fulfilling trees, // 1.7.51 //

children.text: sasakta-citritai ramyai rati-mandira-sundaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: with charming pleasure-pavilions adorned with beautiful paintings,

children.text: golokād āgataṃ pūrvaṃ krīḍārthaṃ śaṅkarasya ca // Jss_1,7.52 //
children.translated_text: having come formerly from <s>Goloka</s> for the play of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, // 1.7.52 //

children.text: vivāhe pariniṣpanne pārvatī-parameśayoḥ /
children.translated_text: upon the completion of the wedding of <s>Pārvatī</s> and <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: rathaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca prayayau kiyad dūraṃ mahā-muniḥ // Jss_1,7.53 //
children.translated_text: Having seen the chariot, the great sage proceeded some distance further // 1.7.53 //

children.text: atīva ramyaṃ ruciraṃ dadarśa śaṅkarāśramam /
children.translated_text: and beheld the exceedingly beautiful and charming hermitage of <s>Śaṅkara</s>,

children.text: ratnendra-sāra-nirmāṇaṃ śiviraiḥ śata-koṭibhiḥ // Jss_1,7.54 //
children.translated_text: constructed of the essence of the finest gems, with hundreds of millions of pavilions, // 1.7.54 //

children.text: mitais tasmāt śata-guṇais tatra sundara-mandiraiḥ /
children.translated_text: measured and a hundred times greater than that, with beautiful temples within,

children.text: yuktaṃ ratna-kapāṭaiś ca ratna-dhātu-vicitritaiḥ // Jss_1,7.55 //
children.translated_text: fitted with gem-paneled doors variegated with mineral pigments of gems, // 1.7.55 //

children.text: parama-stambha-sopānair vajra-miśrair vibhūṣitam /
children.translated_text: adorned with supreme pillars, staircases, and inlaid diamonds,

children.text: dadarśa śiviraṃ śambhoḥ parikhābhis tribhir yutam // Jss_1,7.56 //
children.translated_text: he beheld the encampment of <s>Śambhu</s>, surrounded by three moats, // 1.7.56 //

children.text: durlaghyābhirā-mitrāṇāṃ sugamyābhiḥ satām aho /
children.translated_text: impassable for enemies, yet easily accessible for the virtuous — how wondrous!

children.text: prakāraiś ca tribhir yuktaṃ dhanur lakṣocchritaṃ suta // Jss_1,7.57 //
children.translated_text: Endowed with three ramparts, rising a hundred thousand bow-lengths, O son, // 1.7.57 //

children.text: sammitaṃ saptabhir dvārair nānā-rakṣaka-rakṣitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: fitted with seven gates guarded by various sentinels,

children.text: dhanuḥ-śata-sahasraṃ ca caturasraṃ ca sammitam // Jss_1,7.58 //
children.translated_text: measuring a hundred thousand bow-lengths, square in shape, // 1.7.58 //

children.text: amūlya-ratna-nirmāṇaṃ catuḥ-śālā-śatair yutam /
children.translated_text: constructed of priceless gems, equipped with four hundred halls,

children.text: atīva ramyaṃ purato pura-dvāraṃ dadarśa saḥ // Jss_1,7.59 //
children.translated_text: he beheld before him a most beautiful city-gate. // 1.7.59 //

children.text: purato ratna-bhittau ca kṛtrimaṃ ca suśobhitam /
children.translated_text: Before him on a gem-wall, artfully fashioned and resplendent,

children.text: puṇyaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ ramyaṃ tan-madhye rāsa-maṇḍalam // Jss_1,7.60 //
children.translated_text: [was depicted] the sacred and beautiful <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, and in its midst the <s>rāsa</s>-circle, // 1.7.60 //

children.text: sarvatra rādhā-kṛṣṇaṃ ca pratyekaṃ rati-mandire /
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> everywhere, in each pleasure-pavilion,

children.text: ramyaṃ kuñja-kuṭīrāṇāṃ sahasraṃ sumanoharam // Jss_1,7.61 //
children.translated_text: a thousand charming and most enchanting bower-cottages, // 1.7.61 //

children.text: sugandhi puṣpa-śayyānāṃ sahasraṃ candanokṣitam /
children.translated_text: a thousand fragrant flower-beds sprinkled with sandalwood.

children.text: dvāra-pālaṃ ca tatraiva maṇi-bhadraṃ bhayaṃkaram // Jss_1,7.62 //
children.translated_text: And there as gate-guardian was the fearsome <s>Maṇibhadra</s>, // 1.7.62 //

children.text: tri-śūla-paṭṭiśa-dharaṃ vyāghra-carmāmbaraṃ param /
children.translated_text: bearing a trident and battle-axe, clad in a tiger-skin, supreme.

children.text: taṃ saṃbhāṣya vilokyaivaṃ dvitīya-dvāram īpsitam // Jss_1,7.63 //
children.translated_text: Having greeted and beheld him, he sought the desired second gate // 1.7.63 //

children.text: jagāma ca muni-śreṣṭho dadarśa citram uttamam /
children.translated_text: and the foremost sage went and beheld a wondrous and excellent [scene]:

children.text: kadambānāṃ samūhaṃ ca tan-mūlaṃ ca manoharam // Jss_1,7.64 //
children.translated_text: a grove of <s>Kadamba</s> trees and their enchanting roots, // 1.7.64 //

children.text: ratna-bhitti-samāyuktaṃ kālindī-kūlam uttamam /
children.translated_text: the excellent bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā), set with gem-walls,

children.text: snātaṃ gopī-samūhaṃ ca nagna-sarvāṅgam adbhutam // Jss_1,7.65 //
children.translated_text: a group of <s>gopīs</s> having bathed, wonderfully naked in all limbs, // 1.7.65 //

children.text: kadambāgre ca śrī-kṛṣṇaṃ vastra-puñja-karaṃ param /
children.translated_text: and atop the <s>Kadamba</s> tree, Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> holding the bundle of garments, supreme.

children.text: tatraiva śūla-hastaṃ ca mahā-kālaṃ dadarśa ca // Jss_1,7.66 //
children.translated_text: There too he beheld <s>Mahākāla</s> with trident in hand, // 1.7.66 //

children.text: kṛpāluṃ dvāra-pālaṃ taṃ saṃbhāṣya nārado muniḥ /
children.translated_text: the compassionate gate-guardian; having greeted him, the sage <s>Nārada</s>

children.text: prayayau śīghra-gāmī sa tṛtīya-dvāram uttamam // Jss_1,7.67 //
children.translated_text: proceeded swiftly to the excellent third gate. // 1.7.67 //

children.text: dadarśa tatra purataḥ kṛtrimaṃ vaṭa-mūlakam /
children.translated_text: He beheld there before him an artificial banyan tree at its root,

children.text: gopānāṃ ca samūhaṃ ca pītambara-dharaṃ param // Jss_1,7.68 //
children.translated_text: and a group of cowherds wearing yellow garments, supreme, // 1.7.68 //

children.text: bāla-krīḍāṃ ca kurvantaṃ tan-madhye kṛṣṇam uttamam /
children.translated_text: engaging in childhood sports, and in their midst the excellent <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: brāhmaṇībhiḥ pradattam ca bhuktavantaṃ supāyasam // Jss_1,7.69 //
children.translated_text: having eaten the delicious rice-pudding offered by the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> women. // 1.7.69 //

children.text: kurvantaṃ ca samādhānaṃ muneḥ vāma-kareṇa ca /
children.translated_text: And performing the propitiation of the sage with his left hand,

children.text: gṛhītvā tad-anujñāṃ ca caturthaṃ dvāram īpsitam // Jss_1,7.70 //
children.translated_text: having obtained his permission, he sought the desired fourth gate, // 1.7.70 //

children.text: prayayau brahma-putraś ca dadarśa citram uttamam /
children.translated_text: and the son of <s>Brahmā</s> went and beheld a wondrous and excellent [scene]:

children.text: govardhanaṃ parvataṃ ca tatra kṛṣṇa-kara-sthitam // Jss_1,7.71 //
children.translated_text: mount <s>Govardhana</s>, held aloft by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s hand, // 1.7.71 //

children.text: gokulaṃ gokula-sthānāṃ gopīnāṃ caiva rakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: the protection of <s>Gokula</s>, the dwellers of <s>Gokula</s>, and the <s>gopīs</s>,

children.text: vyākulaṃ gokulaṃ bhītaṃ śakra-vṛṣṭi-bhayena ca // Jss_1,7.72 //
children.translated_text: the agitated and frightened <s>Gokula</s> due to the fear of <s>Indra</s>'s rain, // 1.7.72 //

children.text: abhayaṃ dattavantaṃ ca kṛṣṇaṃ dakṣa-kareṇa ca /
children.translated_text: and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> granting fearlessness with his right hand.

children.text: nandinaṃ dvāra-pālaṃ ca śūla-hastaṃ ca sasmitam // Jss_1,7.73 //
children.translated_text: And <s>Nandin</s>, the gate-guardian, with trident in hand, smiling — // 1.7.73 //

children.text: vilokya prayayau vipraḥ pañcamaṃ dvāṛam uttamam /
children.translated_text: beholding him, the sage proceeded to the excellent fifth gate,

children.text: nānā-kṛtima-citrāḍhyaṃ vīra-bhadrānvitaṃ param // Jss_1,7.74 //
children.translated_text: rich with various artificial paintings, attended by the mighty <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, supreme. // 1.7.74 //

children.text: tatraiva nīpa-mūlaṃ ca yamunākulam eva ca /
children.translated_text: And there, at the base of a <s>Nīpa</s> (Kadamba) tree, the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: kālīya-damanaṃ tatra kṛtimaṃ ca dadarśa ḥa // Jss_1,7.75 //
children.translated_text: and the subduing of <s>Kāliya</s> there, artfully depicted — he beheld it. // 1.7.75 //

children.text: tad dṛṣṭvā sasmitas tuṣṭaḥ ṣaṣṭa-dvāṛaṃ jagāma saḥ /
children.translated_text: Having seen it, smiling and pleased, he went to the sixth gate.

children.text: dvāre niyuktaṃ bālaṃ ca śūla-hastaṃ catur-bhujam // Jss_1,7.76 //
children.translated_text: At the gate, appointed [as guardian], a youth with trident in hand, four-armed, // 1.7.76 //

children.text: ratna-siṃhāsana-sthaṃ ca sasmitaṃ sva-gaṇādhipam /
children.translated_text: seated upon a gem-throne, smiling — the lord of his own hosts (<s>gaṇas</s>).

children.text: dadarśa citraṃ tatraiva mathurā-gamanaṃ hareḥ // Jss_1,7.77 //
children.translated_text: He beheld a painting there depicting <s>Hari</s>'s departure for <s>Mathurā</s>, // 1.7.77 //

children.text: vyākulaṃ gokulaṃ cāpi ratha-sthaṃ śaraṇaṃ harim // Jss_1,7.78/ //
children.translated_text: the agitated <s>Gokula</s>, and <s>Hari</s> the refuge, seated upon the chariot, // 1.7.78 //

body.translated_text: the lamentation of the <s>gopikās</s> and of <s>Yaśodā</s> and <s>Nanda</s> likewise,

children.text: akrūraṃ ca tathā nandaṃ nirānandaṃ śucākulam /
children.translated_text: <s>Akrūra</s> and likewise <s>Nanda</s>, joyless and overwhelmed with grief.

children.text: tad dṛṣṭvā saptama-dvāraṃ dvāra-pālaṃ dadarśa saḥ // Jss_1,7.79 //
children.translated_text: Having seen that, he beheld the seventh gate and its gate-guardian, // 1.7.79 //

children.text: citraṃ kautuka-yuktaṃ ca mathurāyāḥ praveśanam /
children.translated_text: a painting full of wonder — the entry into <s>Mathurā</s>,

children.text: sabalaṃ gopa-sahitaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇaṃ prakṛteḥ param // Jss_1,7.80 //
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, supreme beyond <s>Prakṛti</s>, accompanied by <s>Balarāma</s> and cowherds, // 1.7.80 //

children.text: mathurā-nāgarībhiś ca bālakair vānirargalaiḥ /
children.translated_text: by the women of <s>Mathurā</s> and boys and unrestricted crowds,

children.text: vīkṣantaṃ sādaraṃ sarvair nagara-sthair manoharam // Jss_1,7.81 //
children.translated_text: all the city-dwellers gazing upon the enchanting one with affection, // 1.7.81 //

children.text: dhanur bhaṅgaṃ tathā śaṃbhoḥ kaṃsādi-nidhanādikam /
children.translated_text: the breaking of <s>Śambhu</s>'s bow, the slaying of <s>Kaṃsa</s> and others,

children.text: sabhāryaṃ vasudevaṃ ca nigaḍān muktam īpsitam // Jss_1,7.82 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Vasudeva</s> with his wife, freed from his shackles as desired, // 1.7.82 //

children.text: dvāre niyuktaṃ deveśaṃ gaṇeśaṃ gaṇa-saṃyutam /
children.translated_text: and appointed at the gate, the Lord of gods, <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, surrounded by his hosts,

children.text: dhyāna-sthaṃ ca vibhāntaṃ ca śuddha-sphaṭika-mālayā // Jss_1,7.83 //
children.translated_text: seated in meditation, radiant, with a rosary of pure crystal, // 1.7.83 //

children.text: japantaṃ paramaṃ śuddhaṃ brahma-jyotiḥ sanātanam /
children.translated_text: chanting the supreme and pure <s>Brahman</s>, the eternal light,

children.text: nirliptaṃ nirguṇaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ paramaṃ prakṛteḥ param // Jss_1,7.84 //
children.translated_text: the untainted, quality-less <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, supreme, beyond <s>Prakṛti</s>. // 1.7.84 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā taṃ ca sura-śreṣṭhaṃ muni-śreṣṭho 'pi nāradaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having beheld that foremost of gods, the foremost sage <s>Nārada</s>

children.text: sāma-vedokta-stotreṇa puṣṭāva parameśvaram /
children.translated_text: praised <s>Parameśvara</s> with a hymn spoken in the <s>Sāma Veda</s>,

children.text: sāśru-netraḥ pulakito bhakti-namrātmakaṃdharaḥ // Jss_1,7.85 //
children.translated_text: eyes filled with tears, body thrilled with horripilation, neck bowed in devotion. // 1.7.85 //

body.translated_text: Now, the hymn to <s>Gaṇapati</s>:

children.text: bho gaṇeśa sura-śreṣṭha lambodara parāt para /
children.translated_text: O <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, foremost of the gods, O pot-bellied one (<s>Lambodara</s>), supreme beyond the supreme,

children.text: heramba maṅgalārambha gaja-vaktra tri-locana // Jss_1,7.86 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Heramba</s>, auspicious beginning, elephant-faced, three-eyed, // 1.7.86 //

children.text: muktida śubhada śrīda śrīdhara-smaraṇe rata /
children.translated_text: bestower of liberation, bestower of auspiciousness, bestower of prosperity, devoted to the remembrance of <s>Śrīdhara</s> (Viṣṇu),

children.text: paramānanda parama pārvatī-nandana svayam // Jss_1,7.87 //
children.translated_text: O supreme bliss, O supreme one, O son of <s>Pārvatī</s>, self-born, // 1.7.87 //

children.text: sarvatra pūjya sarveśa jagat-pūjya mahā-mate /
children.translated_text: worshipped everywhere, lord of all, venerated by the world, O great-minded one,

children.text: jagad-guro jagan-nātha jagad-īśa namo 'stu te //Jss_1,7.88 //
children.translated_text: O teacher of the world, lord of the world, ruler of the world — salutations to you! // 1.7.88 //

children.text: yat-pūjā sarva-parato yaḥ stutaḥ sarva-yogibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Whose worship comes before all others, who is praised by all <s>yogins</s>,

children.text: yaḥ pūjitaḥ surendraiś ca munīndrais taṃ namāmy aham // Jss_1,7.89 //
children.translated_text: who is worshipped by the lords of gods and the lords of sages — to him I bow. // 1.7.89 //

children.text: paramārādhanenaiva kṛṣṇasya paramātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the supreme adoration of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Self,

children.text: puṇyakena vratenaiva yaṃ prāpa pārvatī satī // Jss_1,7.90 //
children.translated_text: and through the auspicious vow, whom the chaste <s>Pārvatī</s> obtained — // 1.7.90 //

children.text: taṃ namāmi sura-śreṣṭhaṃ sarva-śreṣṭhaṃ gariṣṭhakam /
children.translated_text: to that foremost of gods, greatest of all, most venerable,

children.text: jñāni-śreṣṭhaṃ variṣṭhaṃ ca taṃ namāmi gaṇeśvaram // Jss_1,7.91 //
children.translated_text: foremost among the wise, most excellent — to that lord of hosts (<s>Gaṇeśvara</s>) I bow. // 1.7.91 //

children.text: ity evam uktvā devarṣis tatraivāntar dadhe vibhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the divine sage, the all-pervading one, disappeared right there.

children.text: nāradaḥ prayayau śīghram īśvarābhyantaraṃ mudā // Jss_1,7.92 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s> proceeded swiftly into the inner sanctum of the Lord with delight. // 1.7.92 //

children.text: idaṃ lambodara-stotraṃ nāradena kṛtaṃ purā /
children.translated_text: This hymn to <s>Lambodara</s> (Gaṇeśa) was composed by <s>Nārada</s> in ancient times;

children.text: pūjā-kāle paṭhen nityaṃ jayas tasya pade pade // Jss_1,7.93 //
children.translated_text: one who recites it daily at the time of worship shall have victory at every step. // 1.7.93 //

children.text: saṃkalpitaṃ paṭhed yo hi varṣam ekaṃ susaṃyataḥ /
children.translated_text: One who recites it with resolve for one year with self-control

children.text: viśiṣṭa-putraṃ labhate paraṃ kṛṣṇa-parāyaṇam // Jss_1,7.94 //
children.translated_text: obtains a distinguished son, supremely devoted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, // 1.7.94 //

children.text: yaśasvinaṃ ca vidvāṃsaṃ dhaninaṃ cira-jīvinam /
children.translated_text: famous, learned, wealthy, and long-lived.

children.text: vighna-nāśo bhavet tasya mahaiśvaryaṃ yaśo 'malam /
children.translated_text: Obstacles are destroyed for him, great sovereignty and spotless fame [arise],

children.text: ihaiva ca sukhaṃ bhaktyānte yāti hareḥ padam // Jss_1,7.95 //
children.translated_text: and happiness here through devotion, and at the end he attains the abode of <s>Hari</s>. // 1.7.95 //

body.text:
iti śrī-nārada-pañca-rātre jñānāmṛta-sāre prathamaika-rātre
gaṇapati-stotraṃ nāma saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh chapter, called 'The Hymn to <s>Gaṇapati</s>,' in the first night of the <s>Jñānāmṛtasāra</s> within the <s>Nārada Pañcarātra</s>.
Eighth chapter of the first night.

children.text: śrī-vyāsa uvāca
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Vyāsa</s> said:

children.text: atha cābhyantaraṃ gatvā nārado hṛṣṭa-mānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having entered the inner sanctum, <s>Nārada</s>, with a joyful heart,

children.text: dadarśa svāśramaṃ ramyam atīva sumanoharam // Jss_1,8.1 //
children.translated_text: beheld his own hermitage, beautiful and most enchanting. // 1.8.1 //

children.text: payaḥ phena-nibha-śayyā-sahitaṃ ratna-mandiram /
children.translated_text: A gem-palace with couches white as the foam of milk,

children.text: sākṣād gorocanābhaiś ca maṇi-stambhair vibhūṣitam // Jss_1,8.2 //
children.translated_text: adorned with gem-pillars resembling real <s>gorocanā</s> (yellow orpiment), // 1.8.2 //

children.text: maṇīndra-sārasopānaiḥ kapāṭaiś ca pariṣkṛtam /
children.translated_text: with staircases of the finest gems and doors, all embellished,

children.text: muktāmāṇikya-hīrāṇāṃ mālā-rāji-virājitam // Jss_1,8.3 //
children.translated_text: resplendent with rows of garlands of pearls, rubies, and diamonds, // 1.8.3 //

children.text: śuddha-sphaṭika-saṃkāśaṃ prāṅgaṇaṃ maṇi-saṃskṛtam /
children.translated_text: a courtyard resembling pure crystal, paved with gems,

children.text: sundaraṃ mandira-cayaṃ sad-ratna-kalaśojjvalam // Jss_1,8.4 //
children.translated_text: a beautiful array of temples brilliant with pinnacles of precious gems, // 1.8.4 //

children.text: ratna-patra-paṭākīrṇaṃ vahni-śuddhāṃśukānvitam /
children.translated_text: strewn with gem-leaf banners, draped with fire-purified fabrics,

children.text: sudhānāṃ ca madhūnām ca pūrṇa-kumbhakaṃ śataṃ śatam // Jss_1,8.5 //
children.translated_text: hundreds upon hundreds of vessels full of nectar and honey, // 1.8.5 //

children.text: dāsa-dāsī-samūhaiś ca ratnālaṅkāra-bhūṣitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: with throngs of male and female servants adorned with gem-ornaments,

children.text: pārvatī-priya-saṅgaiś ca sva-karmākula-saṅkalpam // Jss_1,8.6 //
children.translated_text: with the beloved companions of <s>Pārvatī</s>, [all] occupied with their duties. // 1.8.6 //

children.text: tad dṛṣṭvā ca muni-śreṣṭhas tat parābhyantaraṃ yayau /
children.translated_text: Having seen that, the foremost sage went further inside,

children.text: ratna-siṃhāsana-sthaṃ ca śaṅkaraṃ ca dadarśa saḥ // Jss_1,8.7 //
children.translated_text: and beheld <s>Śaṅkara</s> seated upon a gem-throne. // 1.8.7 //

children.text: vyāghra-carmāmbara-dharaṃ sasmitaṃ candra-śekharam /
children.translated_text: Wearing a tiger-skin garment, smiling, with the crescent moon on his crest,

children.text: prasanna-vadanaṃ svacchaṃ śāntaṃ śrīmantam īśvaram // Jss_1,8.8 //
children.translated_text: of serene countenance, pure, peaceful, glorious, the Lord, // 1.8.8 //

children.text: vibhūti-bhūṣitāṅgaṃ ca paraṃ gaṅgā-jaṭā-dharam /
children.translated_text: his limbs adorned with sacred ash, supreme, bearing the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in his matted locks,

children.text: bhakta-priyaṃ ca bhakteśaṃ jvalantaṃ brahma-tejasā // Jss_1,8.9 //
children.translated_text: dear to his devotees, lord of devotees, blazing with the radiance of <s>Brahman</s>, // 1.8.9 //

children.text: tri-netraṃ pañca-vaktraṃ ca koṭi-candra-sama-prabham /
children.translated_text: three-eyed, five-faced, radiant as ten million moons,

children.text: japantaṃ paramātmānaṃ brahma jyotiḥ sanātanam // Jss_1,8.10 //
children.translated_text: chanting the Supreme Self, <s>Brahman</s>, the eternal light, // 1.8.10 //

children.text: nirliptaṃ ca nirīhaṃ ca dātāraṃ sarva-sampadām /
children.translated_text: untainted, desireless, the bestower of all prosperity,

children.text: svecchā-mayaṃ sarva-bījaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇaṃ prakṛteḥ paraṃ // Jss_1,8.11 //
children.translated_text: self-willed, the seed of all, Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, supreme beyond <s>Prakṛti</s>, // 1.8.11 //

children.text: siddhendraiś ca munīndraiś ca devendraiḥ parisevitam /
children.translated_text: attended by the lords of <s>siddhas</s>, lords of sages, and lords of gods,

children.text: pārśvada-pravara-śreṣṭha-sevitaṃ śveta-cāmaraiḥ // Jss_1,8.12 //
children.translated_text: served by the best foremost attendants with white <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks), // 1.8.12 //

children.text: durgā-sevita-pādābjaṃ bhadra-kālī-pariṣṭutam /
children.translated_text: his lotus-feet served by <s>Durgā</s>, praised by <s>Bhadrakālī</s>,

children.text: purato hi vasantaṃ taṃ skandaṃ gaṇa-patīm tathā // Jss_1,8.13 //
children.translated_text: and before him were seated <s>Skanda</s> and <s>Gaṇapati</s> as well. // 1.8.13 //

children.text: gale baddhvā ca vasanaṃ bhakti-namrātmakaṃdharaḥ /
children.translated_text: Tying a cloth around his neck, with his neck bowed in devotion,

children.text: yogīndraṃ sva-guruṃ śaṃbhuṃ śirasā praṇanāma saḥ // Jss_1,8.14 //
children.translated_text: he bowed his head before <s>Śambhu</s>, the lord of <s>yogins</s>, his own <s>guru</s>. // 1.8.14 //

children.text: tuṣṭāva parayā bhaktyā devarṣir jagatāṃ patim /
children.translated_text: With supreme devotion, the divine sage praised the lord of the worlds,

children.text: sva-guruṃ ca paśu-patiṃ vedoktena stavena ca // Jss_1,8.15 //
children.translated_text: and his own <s>Guru</s>, the Lord of creatures (<s>Paśupati</s>), with a hymn prescribed by the <s>Vedas</s>. // 1.8.15 //

children.text: śrī-nārada uvāca
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: namas tubhyaṃ jagan-nātha mama nātha mama prabho /
children.translated_text: 'Salutations to you, O Lord of the universe, my Lord, my Master,

children.text: bhava-rūpa-taror bīja phala-rūpa phala-prada // Jss_1,8.16 //
children.translated_text: O seed of the tree whose form is existence, O bestower of fruit whose form is the fruit! // 1.8.16 //

children.text: abījaja praja prāja sarva-bīja namo 'stu te /
children.translated_text: O unborn one, O progenitor, O primordial wise one, O seed of all — salutations to you!

children.text: sad-bhāva paramābhāva vibhāva bhāvanāśraya // Jss_1,8.17 //
children.translated_text: O essence of true being, O supreme transcendence, O source of manifestation, O refuge of contemplation! // 1.8.17 //

children.text: bhaveśa bhava-bandheśa bhāvābdhināvināyaka /
children.translated_text: O Lord of existence, O Lord of the bonds of existence, O helmsman of the ship on the ocean of becoming!

children.text: sarvādhāra nirādhāra sādhāra dharaṇī-dhara // Jss_1,8.18 //
children.translated_text: O support of all, O one without support, O support [itself], O bearer of the earth! // 1.8.18 //

children.text: veda-vidyādhārādhāra gaṅādhara namo 'stu te /
children.translated_text: O support of the support of the <s>Vedas</s> and learning, O bearer of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — salutations to you!

children.text: jayeśa vijayādhāra jaya-bīja jayātmaka // Jss_1,8.19 //
children.translated_text: O Lord of victory, O foundation of triumph, O seed of victory, O one whose nature is victory! // 1.8.19 //

body.translated_text: O origin of the universe, O bliss of victory, O bliss of all — salutations to you!'

children.text: ity evam uktvā devarṣiḥ śambhoś ca purataḥ sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the divine sage stood before <s>Śambhu</s>;

children.text: prasanna-vadanaḥ śrīmān bhagavāṃs tam uvāca saḥ // Jss_1,8.20 //
children.translated_text: with a pleased countenance, the glorious Blessed Lord spoke to him: // 1.8.20 //

children.text: śrī-mahā-deva uvāca
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Mahādeva</s> said:

children.text: varaṃ vṛṇu mahā-bhāga yat te manasi vartate /
children.translated_text: 'Choose a boon, O greatly fortunate one — whatever is in your mind;

children.text: dāsyāmi tvāṃ dhruvaṃ putra dātāhaṃ sarva-saṃpadām // Jss_1,8.21 //
children.translated_text: I shall surely grant it to you, O son — I am the bestower of all prosperity. // 1.8.21 //

children.text: sukhaṃ muktiṃ harer bhaktiṃ niścalām avināśinīm /
children.translated_text: Happiness, liberation, unwavering and imperishable devotion to <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: hareḥ pādaṃ tad-dāsyaṃ sālokyādi-catuṣṭayam // Jss_1,8.22 //
children.translated_text: the abode of <s>Hari</s>, servitude to Him, the four [types of liberation] beginning with <s>sālokya</s> (dwelling in His realm), // 1.8.22 //

children.text: indratvam amaratvaṃ vā yamatvam anileśvaram /
children.translated_text: the status of <s>Indra</s>, immortality, the status of <s>Yama</s>, lordship over the wind,

children.text: prajā-patitvaṃ brahmatvaṃ siddhatvaṃ siddha-sādhanam // Jss_1,8.23 //
children.translated_text: the status of <s>Prajāpati</s>, the status of <s>Brahmā</s>, the state of a <s>siddha</s> (perfected being), the means to perfection, // 1.8.23 //

children.text: siddhaiśvaryaṃ siddhi-bījaṃ veda-vidyādhipaṃ param /
children.translated_text: the sovereignty of the <s>siddhas</s>, the seed of perfection, supreme lordship over the <s>Vedas</s> and learning,

children.text: aṇimādika-siddhiṃ ca mano-yāyitvam īpsitam // Jss_1,8.24 //
children.translated_text: the <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers) beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (becoming minute), and the desired ability to travel with the mind — // 1.8.24 //

children.text: hareḥ padaṃ ca gamanaṃ sa-śarīreṇa līlayā /
children.translated_text: going to the abode of <s>Hari</s> bodily and playfully —

children.text: eteṣu vāñchitārtheṣu kiṃ vā te vāñchitaṃ suta // Jss_1,8.25 //
children.translated_text: among these desired objects, what is your wish, O son? // 1.8.25 //

body.text: tan me brūhi muni-śreṣṭha sarvaṃ dātum ahaṃ kṣamaḥ /
body.translated_text: Tell me, O best of sages — I am capable of giving everything.'

body.text: śaṅkarasya vacaḥ śrutvā tam uvāca mahā-muniḥ // Jss_1,8.26 //
body.translated_text: Having heard <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s words, the great sage spoke to him: // 1.8.26 //

children.text: śrī-nārada uvāca
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: dehi me hari-bhaktiṃ ca tan-nāma-sevane ruciḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Give me devotion to <s>Hari</s> and a taste for serving His name;

children.text: ati-tṛṣṇā guṇākhyāne nityam astu mameśvara // Jss_1,8.27 //
children.translated_text: may there always be intense longing in me for narrating [His] qualities, O Lord.' // 1.8.27 //

children.text: nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā jahāsa śaṅkaraḥ svayam /
children.translated_text: Having heard <s>Nārada</s>'s words, <s>Śaṅkara</s> himself laughed,

children.text: pārvatī bhadra-kālī ca kārttikeyo gaṇeśvaraḥ // Jss_1,8.28 //
children.translated_text: as did <s>Pārvatī</s>, <s>Bhadrakālī</s>, <s>Kārtikeya</s>, and <s>Gaṇeśvara</s>. // 1.8.28 //

children.text: sarvaṃ dadau mahā-devo nāradāya ca dhīmate /
children.translated_text: <s>Mahādeva</s> gave everything to the wise <s>Nārada</s> —

children.text: sarva-pradas tu sarveśaḥ sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇaḥ // Jss_1,8.29 //
children.translated_text: the giver of all, the Lord of all, the cause of all causes. // 1.8.29 //

children.text: nāradena kṛtaṃ stotraṃ nityaṃ yaḥ prapaṭhet śuciḥ /
children.translated_text: Whoever recites daily with purity the hymn composed by <s>Nārada</s>,

children.text: hari-bhaktir bhavet tasya tan-nāmni guṇato ruciḥ // Jss_1,8.30 //
children.translated_text: devotion to <s>Hari</s> shall arise in him, and a taste for His name and qualities. // 1.8.30 //

children.text: daśa-vāra-japenaiva stotra-siddhir bhaven nṛṇām /
children.translated_text: By reciting ten times, the efficacy of the hymn is attained by people;

children.text: sarva-siddhir bhavet tasya siddha-stotro bhaved yadi // Jss_1,8.31 //
children.translated_text: all perfections accrue to the one for whom the hymn has become efficacious. // 1.8.31 //

children.text: iha prāpnoti lakṣmīṃ ca niścalāṃ lakṣa-pauruṣīm /
children.translated_text: In this [life] one obtains unwavering <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) with a hundred-thousand-fold power,

children.text: pari-pūrṇam ahaiśvaryam ante yāti hareḥ padam // Jss_1,8.32 //
children.translated_text: complete sovereignty, and at the end goes to the abode of <s>Hari</s>. // 1.8.32 //

children.text: putraṃ viśiṣṭaṃ labhate hari-bhaktaṃ jitendriyam /
children.translated_text: One obtains a distinguished son, a devotee of <s>Hari</s>, with senses conquered,

children.text: susādhyāṃ suvinītāṃ suvratāṃ ca pati-vratām // Jss_1,8.33 //
children.translated_text: and a wife who is virtuous, well-mannered, of excellent vows, devoted to her husband. // 1.8.33 //

children.text: prajāṃ bhūmiṃ yaśaḥ kīrtiṃ vidyāṃ sa-kavitāṃ labhet /
children.translated_text: One obtains progeny, land, fame, renown, learning, and poetic skill;

children.text: prasūyate mahā-bandhyā varṣam ekaṃ śṛṇoti cet // Jss_1,8.34 //
children.translated_text: even a woman long barren conceives if she hears [the hymn] for one year. // 1.8.34 //

children.text: galat-kuṣṭhī mahā-rogī sadyo rogāt pramucyate /
children.translated_text: One afflicted with leprosy or great disease is immediately freed from illness;

children.text: dhanī mahā-daridraś ca kṛpaṇaḥ satyavān bhavet /
children.translated_text: the greatly destitute becomes wealthy, and the miserly becomes truthful;

children.text: viprad-grasto rāja-baddho mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ // Jss_1,8.35 //
children.translated_text: one seized by an adversary or imprisoned by a king is freed — there is no doubt in this. // 1.8.35 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth chapter of the first night of the <s>Jñānāmṛtasāra</s> within the <s>Nārada Pañcarātra</s>.
Ninth chapter of the first night.

children.text: śrī-vyāsa uvāca
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Vyāsa</s> said:

children.text: varaṃ datvā mahā-devo bhaktyā taṃ brāhmaṇātithim /
children.translated_text: Having granted the boon, <s>Mahādeva</s>, with devotion, to that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> guest,

children.text: pūjāṃ cakāra vedoktāṃ svayaṃ veda-vidāṃ varaḥ // Jss_1,9.1 //
children.translated_text: performed the worship prescribed by the <s>Vedas</s> — he himself, the best among knowers of the <s>Vedas</s>. // 1.9.1 //

children.text: bhuktvā pītvā muni-śreṣṭho mahā-devasya mandire /
children.translated_text: Having eaten and drunk, the best of sages, in the abode of <s>Mahādeva</s>,

children.text: tiṣṭhann upāsānāṃ cakre pārvatī-parameśayoḥ // Jss_1,9.2 //
children.translated_text: while residing, performed worship of <s>Pārvatī</s> and <s>Parameśvara</s>. // 1.9.2 //

children.text: ekadā cira-kālānte tam uvāca mahā-munim /
children.translated_text: One day, after a long time, <s>Mahādeva</s> spoke to the great sage

children.text: mahā-devaḥ sabhā-madhye kṛpayā ca kṛpā-nidhiḥ // Jss_1,9.3 //
children.translated_text: in the midst of the assembly, with compassion — He, the treasury of mercy: // 1.9.3 //

children.text: śrī-mahā-deva uvāca
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Mahādeva</s> said:

children.text: kiṃ vā te vāñchitaṃ vatsa brūhi māṃ yadi rocate /
children.translated_text: 'What do you desire, O dear child? Tell me if it pleases you;

children.text: varo dattaḥ kim aparaṃ yat te manasi vartate // Jss_1,9.4 //
children.translated_text: a boon has been given — what else is in your mind?' // 1.9.4 //

children.text: mahā-deva-vacaḥ śrutvā tam uvāca mahā-muniḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of <s>Mahādeva</s>, the great sage spoke to Him —

children.text: kailāse ca sabhā-madhye yat tan-manasi vāñchitam // Jss_1,9.5 //
children.translated_text: on <s>Kailāsa</s>, in the midst of the assembly — what was desired in his mind: // 1.9.5 //

children.text: śrī-nārada uvāca
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: jñānam ādhyātmikaṃ nāma veda-sāraṃ manoharam /
children.translated_text: 'The spiritual knowledge (<s>ādhyātmika-jñāna</s>) — the essence of the <s>Vedas</s>, delightful,

children.text: hari-bhakti-pradaṃ jñānaṃ muktidaṃ jñānam īpsitam // Jss_1,9.6 //
children.translated_text: knowledge that bestows devotion to <s>Hari</s>, knowledge that grants liberation, the desired knowledge, // 1.9.6 //

children.text: yoga-yuktaṃ ca yaj jñānaṃ jñānaṃ yat siddhidaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: knowledge conjoined with <s>yoga</s>, and knowledge that bestows <s>siddhis</s> (perfections) —

children.text: saṃsāra-viṣaya-jñānam eva pañca-vidhaṃ smṛtam // Jss_1,9.7 //
children.translated_text: these are remembered as the five kinds of knowledge pertaining to worldly experience. // 1.9.7 //

children.text: āśramāṇāṃ samācāraṃ teṣāṃ dharma-pariṣkṛtam /
children.translated_text: The conduct of the <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life), their dharma-observances,

children.text: vidhavānāṃ ca bhikṣūṇāṃ yatīnāṃ brahma-cāriṇāṃ // Jss_1,9.8 //
children.translated_text: [the dharma] of widows, of mendicants, of <s>yatis</s> (ascetics), of <s>brahmacārins</s> (celibate students); // 1.9.8 //

children.text: pūjā-vidhānaṃ kṛṣṇasya tat-stotraṃ kavacaṃ manum /
children.translated_text: the procedure of worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, His hymns, <s>kavaca</s>, and <s>mantra</s>,

children.text: puraścaryā-vidhānaṃ ca sarvāhnikam abhīpsitam // Jss_1,9.9 //
children.translated_text: the procedure for <s>puraścarya</s> (preliminary practices), and the desired daily rituals; // 1.9.9 //

children.text: jīva-karma-vipākaṃ ca karma-mūla-nikṛntanam /
children.translated_text: the ripening of the <s>jīva</s>'s (soul's) <s>karma</s>, and the cutting of the root of <s>karma</s>;

children.text: saṃsāra-vāsanāṃ kāṃ vā lakṣaṇaṃ prakṛtīśayoḥ // Jss_1,9.10 //
children.translated_text: what are the impressions of <s>saṃsāra</s> (<s>vāsanā</s>), and the characteristics of <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature) and <s>Īśa</s> (Lord); // 1.9.10 //

children.text: tayoḥ paraṃ vā kiṃ vastu tasyāvatāra-varṇamam /
children.translated_text: what reality is beyond those two, the description of His <s>avatāras</s> (incarnations),

children.text: ko vā tad-aṃśaḥ kaḥ pūrṇaḥ paripūrṇatamaś ca kaḥ // Jss_1,9.11 //
children.translated_text: who is His partial manifestation, who is complete, and who is the most complete; // 1.9.11 //

children.text: nārāyaṇarṣi-kavacaṃ subhadra-pravarāya ca /
children.translated_text: the <s>kavaca</s> of sage <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, which was given to the excellent <s>Subhadra</s> —

children.text: yad dattaṃ kiṃ tad deveśa tad ārādhyaṃ prayatnataḥ // Jss_1,9.12 //
children.translated_text: what is that, O Lord of gods? That which is to be worshipped with effort; // 1.9.12 //

children.text: mayā jñānaṃm anāpṛṣṭhaṃ yad yad asti surottama /
children.translated_text: whatever knowledge I have not yet asked about, O best of gods,

children.text: tan me kathaya tattvena mām evānugrahaṃ kuru // Jss_1,9.13 //
children.translated_text: tell me that in truth — bestow your grace upon me. // 1.9.13 //

children.text: guroś ca jñānodgiraṇāj jñānaṃ syān mantra-tantrayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the <s>Guru</s>'s utterance of knowledge, knowledge arises regarding <s>mantra</s> and <s>tantra</s>;

children.text: tat tantraṃ sa ca mantraḥ syād yato bhaktir adhokṣaje // Jss_1,9.14 //
children.translated_text: that is the <s>tantra</s> and that is the <s>mantra</s> from which devotion to <s>Adhokṣaja</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) [arises]. // 1.9.14 //

children.text: jñānaṃ syād viduṣāṃ kiṃcid veda-vyākhyāna-cintayā /
children.translated_text: Knowledge may arise for the learned through reflection on the exposition of the <s>Vedas</s>,

children.text: svayaṃ bhavān veda-kartā jñānādhiṣṭhātṛ-devatā // Jss_1,9.15 //
children.translated_text: but you yourself are the author of the <s>Vedas</s>, the presiding deity of knowledge.' // 1.9.15 //

children.text: nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā sasmitaḥ pārvatī-patiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard <s>Nārada</s>'s words, the husband of <s>Pārvatī</s>, smiling,

children.text: nirīkṣya pārvatī-vaktraṃ gaja-vaktram uvāca saḥ // Jss_1,9.16 //
children.translated_text: looked at the face of <s>Pārvatī</s> and spoke to the elephant-faced one (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>): // 1.9.16 //

body.translated_text: Now, the receiving of instruction by <s>Nārada</s>:

children.text: śrī-mahā-deva uvāca
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Mahādeva</s> said:

children.text: aho ananta-dāsānāṃ māhātmyaṃ paramādbhutam /
children.translated_text: 'Ah, the glory of the servants of the Infinite One (<s>Ananta</s>) is most wonderful!

children.text: kurvanty ahaitukīṃ bhaktiṃ ye ca śaśvad dhareḥ pade // Jss_1,9.17 //
children.translated_text: They who perpetually offer causeless devotion at the feet of <s>Hari</s> — // 1.9.17 //

children.text: padma-nābha-pāda-padmaṃ padmā-padmeśvarārcitam /
children.translated_text: those who day and night meditate upon the lotus feet of <s>Padmanābha</s>, which are worshipped by <s>Padmā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) and the Lord of <s>Padmā</s>,

children.text: divāniśaṃ ye dhyāyante śeṣādi-sura-vanditam // Jss_1,9.18 //
children.translated_text: which are venerated by <s>Śeṣa</s> and the gods — // 1.9.18 //

children.text: ālāpaṃ gātra-saṃsparśaṃ pāda-reṇum abhīpsitam /
children.translated_text: their conversation, the touch of their limbs, the dust of their feet — these desired things

children.text: vāñchanty eva hi tīrthāni vasudhā cātma-śuddhaye // Jss_1,9.19 //
children.translated_text: are longed for by the sacred <s>tīrthas</s> (pilgrimage sites) and by the earth herself, for self-purification. // 1.9.19 //

children.text: kṛṣṇa-mantropāsakānāṃ śuddhaṃ pādodakaṃ suta /
children.translated_text: The pure foot-water of the worshippers of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s <s>mantra</s>, O son,

children.text: punāti sarva-tīrthāni vasudhām api pārvati // Jss_1,9.20 //
children.translated_text: purifies all <s>tīrthas</s> and the earth itself, O <s>Pārvatī</s>. // 1.9.20 //

children.text: kṛṣṇa-mantro dvija-mukhād yasya karṇaṃ prayāti ca /
children.translated_text: The <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-<s>mantra</s>, when it enters one's ear from the mouth of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>,

children.text: taṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ jagat-pūtaṃ pravadanti purā-vidaḥ // Jss_1,9.21 //
children.translated_text: that person — the knowers of ancient lore declare him a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, a purifier of the world. // 1.9.21 //

children.text: mantra-grahaṇa-mātreṇa naro nārāyanātmakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Merely by receiving the <s>mantra</s>, a person becomes identified with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;

children.text: punāti līlā-mātreṇa puruṣāṇāṃ śataṃ śatam // Jss_1,9.22 //
children.translated_text: he purifies effortlessly hundreds upon hundreds of people. // 1.9.22 //

children.text: yaj janma-mātrāt pūtaṃ ca tat pitṛṇāṃ śataṃ śatam /
children.translated_text: By his mere birth, hundreds upon hundreds of his ancestors are purified;

children.text: prayāti sadyo golokaṃ karma-bhogāt pramucyate // Jss_1,9.23 //
children.translated_text: he goes immediately to <s>Goloka</s> and is freed from the experience of <s>karma</s>. // 1.9.23 //

children.text: mātā-mahādikān sapta janma-mātrāt samuddharet /
children.translated_text: Seven [generations] of maternal ancestors he uplifts by his mere birth;

children.text: yat kanyāṃ pratigṛhṇāti tasya saptāvalīlayā // Jss_1,9.24 //
children.translated_text: and [the family of] one who accepts his daughter — seven [generations] effortlessly. // 1.9.24 //

children.text: mātaraṃ tat-praśūṃ bhāryāṃ putrāc ca sapta-pūruṣam /
children.translated_text: His mother, her parents, his wife, and seven generations from his son,

children.text: bhrātaraṃ bhaginīṃ kanyāṃ kṛṣṇa-bhaktaḥ samuddharet // Jss_1,9.24 //
children.translated_text: his brother, sister, and daughter — a devotee of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> uplifts [them all]. // 1.9.25 //

children.text: sa snātaḥ sarva-tīrtheṣu sarva-yajñeṣu dīkṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: He is bathed in all <s>tīrthas</s>, initiated in all <s>yajñas</s> (sacrifices);

children.text: phalaṃ sa lebhe pūjānāṃ vratī sarva-vrateṣu ca // Jss_1,9.26 //
children.translated_text: he has obtained the fruit of all worship, and is a votary in all <s>vratas</s> (vows). // 1.9.26 //

children.text: viṣṇu-mantraṃ yo labhet vaiṣṇavāc ca dvijottamāt /
children.translated_text: One who receives the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-<s>mantra</s> from a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, a best of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: koṭi-janmārjitāt pāpān mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ // Jss_1,9.27 //
children.translated_text: is freed from sins accumulated over ten million births — there is no doubt in this. // 1.9.27 //

children.text: kṛṣṇa-mantropāsakānāṃ sadyo darśana-mātrataḥ /
children.translated_text: By merely seeing the worshippers of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s <s>mantra</s>,

children.text: śata-janmārjitāt pāpān mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ // Jss_1,9.28 //
children.translated_text: one is freed from sins accumulated over a hundred births — there is no doubt in this. // 1.9.28 //

children.text: vaiṣṇavād darśanenaiva sparśanena ca pārvati /
children.translated_text: By the sight of a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> and by his touch, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,

children.text: sadyaḥ pūtaṃ jalaṃ vahnir jagat pūtaḥ samīraṇaḥ // Jss_1,9.29 //
children.translated_text: water, fire, the world, and the wind are instantly purified. // 1.9.29 //

children.text: darśanaṃ vaiṣṇavānāṃ ca devā vāñchanti nityaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The gods themselves perpetually desire the sight of <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>;

children.text: na vaiṣṇavāt paraḥ pūto viśveṣu nikhileṣu ca // Jss_1,9.30 //
children.translated_text: there is none purer than a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> in all the worlds. // 1.9.30 //

children.text: ity uktvā saṅkaraḥ śīghraṃ nāradena sahātmajaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, together with his son and <s>Nārada</s>, quickly

children.text: yayau mandākinī-tīraṃ nīraṃ kṣīropamaṃ param // Jss_1,9.31 //
children.translated_text: went to the bank of the <s>Mandākinī</s>, whose water is supreme, resembling milk. // 1.9.31 //

children.text: tatra snāto mahā-devī nāradaś ca mahā-muniḥ /
children.translated_text: There, <s>Mahādevī</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>) and <s>Nārada</s> the great sage bathed;

children.text: samācāntaḥ śucis tatra dhṛtvā dhaute ca vāsavī // Jss_1,9.32 //
children.translated_text: having performed <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping), pure, wearing washed garments there, // 1.9.32 //

children.text: kṛṣṇa-mantraṃ dadau tasmai nāradāya maheśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Maheśvara</s> gave the <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-<s>mantra</s> to <s>Nārada</s> —

children.text: paraṃ kapla-taru-varaṃ sarva-siddhi-pradaṃ śuka // Jss_1,9.33 //
children.translated_text: the supreme wish-fulfilling tree (<s>kalpa-taru</s>), bestowing all <s>siddhis</s>, O <s>Śuka</s>. // 1.9.33 //

children.text: lakṣmīr māyā-kāma-bījaṃ ṅentaṃ kṛṣṇa-padaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>māyā</s>, <s>kāma-bīja</s>, the syllable 'ṅ,' the word '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,' then

children.text: jagat-pūta-priyāntaṃ ca mantra-rājaṃ prakīrtitam // Jss_1,9.34 //
children.translated_text: ending with 'purifier of the world, beloved' — [this] is proclaimed as the king of <s>mantras</s>. // 1.9.34 //

children.text: mantraṃ gṛhītvā sa muniḥ śivaṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam /
children.translated_text: Having received the <s>mantra</s>, the sage circumambulated <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: sapta vārān namas kṛtya svātmānaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dadau // Jss_1,9.35 //
children.translated_text: bowed seven times, and offered himself as the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee). // 1.9.35 //

children.text: tat-pāda-padme vikrītamājanma mastakaṃ param /
children.translated_text: At His lotus feet, the sage, filled with devotion, sold his head for all eternity,

children.text: muninā bhakti-yuktena svarga-mandākinī-taṭe // Jss_1,9.36 //
children.translated_text: on the bank of the heavenly <s>Mandākinī</s>. // 1.9.36 //

children.text: etasminn antare vatsa puṣpa-vṛṣṭir babhūva ha /
children.translated_text: At that moment, O child, there was a shower of flowers;

children.text: nāradopari tatraiva suśrāva dundubhir muniḥ // Jss_1,9.37 //
children.translated_text: upon <s>Nārada</s>, right there, the sage heard divine kettledrums. // 1.9.37 //

children.text: nanarta brahmaṇaḥ putro brahma-loke nirāmaye /
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Brahmā</s> danced in <s>Brahmaloka</s>, the abode free from affliction;

children.text: brahmā jagāma tatraiva suprasannaś ca sasmitaḥ // Jss_1,9.38 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> himself came there, well-pleased and smiling. // 1.9.38 //

children.text: putraṃ śubhāśiṣaṃ kṛtvā tuṣṭāva candra-śekharam /
children.translated_text: Having blessed his son with auspicious benedictions, he praised <s>Candraśekhara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>);

children.text: śambhuś ca pūjayām āsa brāhmaṇam atithiṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Śambhu</s> also worshipped the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> guest, and

children.text: śambhuṃ śubhāśiṣaṃ kṛtvā brahma-lokaṃ yayau vidhiḥ // Jss_1,9.39 //
children.translated_text: having blessed <s>Śambhu</s> with auspicious benedictions, <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) returned to <s>Brahmaloka</s>. // 1.9.39 //

body.text:
iti śrī-nārada-pañca-rātre jñānāmṛta-sāre prathamaika-rātre
nāradopadeśa-grahaṇaṃ nāma navamo 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth chapter, called 'The Receiving of Instruction by <s>Nārada</s>,' in the first night of the <s>Jñānāmṛtasāra</s> within the <s>Nārada Pañcarātra</s>.
Tenth chapter of the first night.

children.text: śrī-śuka uvāca
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Śuka</s> said:

children.text: nārado hi mahā-jñānī devarṣir brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nārada</s>, the great knower, divine sage, son of <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: sarva-veda-vidāṃ śreṣṭho gariṣṭhaś ca variṣṭhakaḥ // Jss_1,10.1 //
children.translated_text: foremost among all knowers of the <s>Vedas</s>, most eminent and most excellent — // 1.10.1 //

children.text: kathaṃ sa nopadiṣṭaś ca jñāna-hīno mahā-muniḥ /
children.translated_text: how is it that he was not instructed, that the great sage was devoid of knowledge?

children.text: tan māṃ bodhaya vibho sandeha-bhañjanaṃ kuru // Jss_1,10.2 //
children.translated_text: Explain that to me, O Lord; dispel my doubt.' // 1.10.2 //

children.text: śrī-vyāsa uvāca
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Vyāsa</s> said:

children.text: nārado brahmaṇaḥ putraḥ purā-kalpe babhūva saḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nārada</s>, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, in a former <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle) —

children.text: sarva-jñānaṃ dadau tasmai vidhātā jagatām api // Jss_1,10.3 //
children.translated_text: the Creator gave him all knowledge, even for the sake of the worlds. // 1.10.3 //

children.text: vedāṃś ca pāṭhayām āsa vedāṅgāny api suvrata /
children.translated_text: He taught him the <s>Vedas</s> and the <s>Vedāṅgas</s> (limbs of the <s>Vedas</s>) as well, O one of excellent vows,

children.text: siddha-vidyāṃ śilpa-vidyāṃ yoga-śāstraṃ purāṇakam // Jss_1,10.4 //
children.translated_text: the knowledge of the <s>siddhas</s>, the knowledge of arts, the science of <s>yoga</s>, and the <s>Purāṇas</s>. // 1.10.4 //

children.text: bhagavān ekadā putraṃ kathayām āsa saṃsadi /
children.translated_text: One day, the Blessed Lord (<s>Brahmā</s>) spoke to his son in the assembly:

children.text: sṛṣṭiṃ kuru mahā-bhāga kṛtvā dāra-parigraham // Jss_1,10.5 //
children.translated_text: "Create progeny, O greatly fortunate one, having taken a wife." // 1.10.5 //

children.text: brahmaṇaś ca vacaḥ śrutvā kopa-raktāsya-locanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of <s>Brahmā</s>, with eyes reddened by anger,

children.text: uvāca pitaraṃ kopāt paraṃ kṛṣṇa-parāyanaḥ // Jss_1,10.6 //
children.translated_text: he spoke to his father in wrath — he, wholly devoted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: // 1.10.6 //

children.text: śrī-nārada uvāca
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: sarveṣām api vandyānāṃ pitā caiva mahā-guruḥ /
children.translated_text: "Among all who are venerable, a father is indeed the great <s>guru</s>;

children.text: jñāna-dātuḥ paro vandyo na bhūto na bhaviṣyati // Jss_1,10.7 //
children.translated_text: but no one greater to venerate than the giver of knowledge has been or ever shall be. // 1.10.7 //

children.text: stana-dātrī garbha-dhātrī sneha-kartrī sadāmbikā /
children.translated_text: A mother who gives the breast, who bears [one] in the womb, who bestows affection —

children.text: janma-dātānna-dātā syāt sneha-kartā pitā sadā // Jss_1,10.8 //
children.translated_text: the birth-giver and the food-giver — the father is always the one who shows affection. // Jss_1,10.8 //

children.text: na kṣamau tau ca pitarau putrasya karma khaṇḍitum /
children.translated_text: Those two parents are not capable of cutting the son's <s>karma</s>;

children.text: karoti sad-guruḥ śiṣya-karma-mūla-nikṛntanam // Jss_1,10.9 //
children.translated_text: but the true <s>guru</s> uproots the very root of the disciple's <s>karma</s>. // Jss_1,10.9 //

children.text: guruś ca jñānodgiraṇāt jñānaṃ syān mantra-tantrayoḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>guru</s> imparts knowledge — knowledge arises from <s>mantra</s> and <s>tantra</s>;

children.text: tat tantraṃ sa ca mantraś ca kṛṣṇa-bhaktir yato bhavet // Jss_1,10.10 //
children.translated_text: that <s>tantra</s> and that <s>mantra</s> are those from which devotion to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> arises. // Jss_1,10.10 //

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa-vimukho bhūtvā viṣaye yasya mānasam /
children.translated_text: One who has turned away from <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> and whose mind dwells on sense-objects —

children.text: viṣam atyamṛtaṃ tyaktvā sa ca mūḍho narādhamaḥ // Jss_1,10.11 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned supreme nectar for poison, he is a fool, the lowest of men. // Jss_1,10.11 //

children.text: sa guruḥ sa pitā vandyaḥ sā mātā sa patiḥ sutaḥ /
children.translated_text: He is the [true] <s>guru</s>, he the [true] father to be honored, she the [true] mother, he the [true] husband and son,

children.text: yo dadāti harau bhaktiṃ karma-mūla-nikṛntanī // Jss_1,10.12 //
children.translated_text: who bestows devotion to <s>Hari</s> — that which uproots the very root of <s>karma</s>. // Jss_1,10.12 //

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa-bhajanaṃ tāta sarva-maṅgala-maṅgalam /
children.translated_text: Worship of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, O dear one, is the blessing of all blessings,

children.text: karmopabhoga-rogaāṇām auṣadhaṃ tan-nikṛntanam // Jss_1,10.13 //
children.translated_text: the medicine that uproots the diseases of <s>karma</s> and its fruition. // Jss_1,10.13 //

children.text: aho jagad-vidhātuś ca dharma-śāstur iyaṃ matiḥ /
children.translated_text: Alas! Such is the mentality of the creator of the world, the lawgiver of <s>dharma</s> —

children.text: svayaṃ māyā-mohitaś ca paraṃ bhraṣṭaṃ karoti ca // Jss_1,10.14 //
children.translated_text: himself deluded by <s>Māyā</s>, he causes others to fall! // Jss_1,10.14 //

children.text: viṣṇus tvāṃ mohitām kṛtvā yuyoja sraṣṭum īśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord, having deluded you, engaged you in creation;

children.text: na dadau svātma-bhaktiṃ tāṃ sva-dāsyaṃ cāti-durlabham // Jss_1,10.15 //
children.translated_text: He did not give you devotion to His own Self, nor His own servitude, which is most rare. // Jss_1,10.15 //

children.text: mātā dadāti putrāya modakaṃ kṣun-nivārakam /
children.translated_text: A mother gives her son a sweetmeat to ward off hunger;

children.text: sa ca bālo na jānāti kathaṃbhūtaṃ ca modakam // Jss_1,10.16 //
children.translated_text: but the child does not know what kind of sweetmeat it is. // Jss_1,10.16 //

children.text: bālakaṃ vañcanaṃ kṛtvā miṣṭaṃ dravyaṃ pradāya saḥ /
children.translated_text: Having deceived the child by giving him a sweet thing,
